tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# Thoughts, notes, open questions for jarodtaylor.com
2	
3	**Companion file:** `CONTENT.md`
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Jarod has 18 years of strong, relevant work (design systems, frontend platforms, developer experience, engineering leadership) and almost none of it is public. His domain has said "coming soon" for years. Searching his name mostly shows other Jarod/Jared Taylors, including one he must never be confused with.
10	
11	He needs one owned home on the web that:
12	1. tells a recruiter or hiring manager who he is in seconds,
13	2. proves his design engineering and frontend systems skill instead of just claiming it, and
14	3. gives him a place to publish writing that LinkedIn and X posts can link to.
15	
16	## Audience
17	
18	1. **Recruiters and hiring managers** (primary). Skimming. Need: role, seniority, proof, availability, contact.
19	2. **Engineering and design leaders / peers.** Reading posts. Need: substance, a reason to follow.
20	3. **Frontend and design engineers.** Will open dev tools and view source. Need: to be impressed by the craft.
21	
22	## Positioning
23	
24	> Designer turned engineer turned engineering leader. For 18 years I've built the work behind the work: design systems, frontend platforms, and developer experience that make whole engineering orgs faster. I've also led the teams that build them, through acquisitions, a bankruptcy, and more reorgs than I can count. These days I'm learning AI the way I learned everything else: hands-on, in public, with an ADHD brain running twenty threads at once.
25	
26	**Four content pillars:** Leading engineering orgs · Design engineering and frontend systems · Developer experience · Learning AI in public.
27	**Honesty rule:** AI is framed as *learning in progress*, never as expertise. Don't add claims that aren't in `CONTENT.md`.
28	
29	## Pages
30	
31	Should this be a single page site? Homepage and Blog? Or best to have standard pages? If standard pages for growth reasons, initial thoughts:
32	
33	* Homepage
34	* About
35	* Blog
36	* Work/Projects/Case Studies? A place where I can do case studies because as a leader at 3 different Fortune 500 I've delivered design systems and component libraries. This was done before the industry was even talking about design systems, tokens, etc. I also will have my personal projects/repos (mainly AI or Design System related) so I'm not sure if this belongs on the same page or something separate? 
37	* Is Contact Me even necessary anymore, or as part of the About Me (and in the footer) I have links to my Email, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, etc? 
38	* Colophon? This site will be like a portfolio piece, so why not have a page giving the details of how it was designed and built. Very similar to what this guy did: https://aarronwalter.com/colophon
39	
40	## Ideas for the site
41	
42	This is not exhaustive. Any new ideas we can come up with should be captured.
43	
44	### Design System Driven
45	
46	I'm an engineering leader with more than a decade of experience building Design Systems, Component Libraries, and Teams that build/curate them at Fortune 500 companies (enterprise companies). This site should demonstrate that. 
47	
48	* **Tokens live in W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) JSON** in the repo, compiled to CSS. This is the source of truth that Figma Variables sync with. Brands should map cleanly to Figma Variable *modes*. Here are some Figma articles:
49	
50	  * [Design token architecture: Structuring tokens for scale](https://www.figma.com/resource-library/design-token-architecture/)
51	  * [Design tokens: How to sync design and code in Figma](https://www.figma.com/resource-library/design-tokens/)
52	* **Design-system components are React (`.tsx`), rendered by Astro.** Pages and layouts stay `.astro`; reusable UI (buttons, tags, cards, nav, section shells, the Remix control) is React so standard `@storybook/react-vite` works with no community plugins.
53	  - Components render **server-side to static HTML by default** (no `client:*` directive). React ships to the browser only for islands that truly need it, so the zero-JS and Lighthouse targets still hold.
54	  - Component styles are **plain CSS, Tailwind, or CSS Modules) that consume tokens only**. No CSS-in-JS runtime, no hard-coded values. This keeps the "tokens, not framework" story honest.
55	
56	* I want to show off the design system, tokens, and engineering side of my experience. So, the idea is one set of markup, completely restyled (not just themed colors, etc. but layout, component changes, spacing, typography, etc) all driven by the token system. A little modern take on the classic 2003 CSS Zen Garden which I actually learned from! My goal is to demonstrate the site from Figma -> Design Tokens (Style Dictionary, or another alternative) -> Storybook -> Website driven by the design system and tokens. We can always backfill Figma and Storybook once we've landed on the brand, design etc. on the website. 
57	
58	* Initial goal would be at least **3 curated brands**: the default brand plus 2 alternates. They must differ in *more than color*: typography, type scale, spacing density, shape/radius, borders, and texture should all be able to change. 
59	
60	* Maybe not v1 but I'd be curious if we could go beyond tokens and even toggle component configurations. For example, let's say we have a Hero on the page with text on the left, an eyebrow, paragraph and a graphic or image on the right. A component built correctly would allow a simple toggle to change the layout of that Hero. Again, this is just an idea, but could be something we explore AFTER v1 of the Remix system. 
61	
62	* Tiered token architecture, visible in the source:
63	
64	  - **Base/knob tier:** the few inputs a brand sets (e.g. base size, scale ratio, density, radius, border weight, fonts, palette).
65	  - **Semantic tier:** derived meanings (background, text, accent, spacing steps, type steps).
66	  - **Component tier:** what components consume.
67	  - Contrasting sections use **semantic surface roles** (e.g. `surface`, `surface-inverse`, `surface-accent`), never hard-coded colors. Each brand decides what each role looks like, and a future dark mode stays possible without a refactor.
68	  - A brand sets **only** the base tier. Everything else is derived. This is what makes Remix v2 (live knobs) possible later, so design for it now.
69	  - While remixing, the visitor can see *what changed*: which tokens changed and that zero markup did (e.g. "14 tokens changed · 0 lines of markup changed").
70	  - Switching brands transitions smoothly and respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
71	  - All brands pass WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on every surface role used on the page. Verify automatically (a script or test), not by eye.
72	  - The chosen brand's tokens must be exportable (e.g. JSON) so the same values drive social graphics, OG images, and slides outside the site.
73	
74	  ### 
75	
76	## Quality bar (non-functional requirements)
77	
78	This is a design engineer's site; the bar is the point.
79	
80	| Area | Requirement |
81	|---|---|
82	| Performance | Lighthouse 100 in Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO on Home and the post template (mobile). Jarod's own work took Tom Ford from 29 to 95; his site can't do worse. |
83	| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA. Full keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic landmarks, skip link, reduced-motion support. |
84	| JavaScript | Minimal. Content pages work with JS off. Only the Remix needs JS. |
85	| Fonts | Self-hosted, subset, no layout shift. |
86	| Responsive | Excellent from 360px to wide desktop. No horizontal scroll. |
87	| Source quality | Clean, readable HTML and CSS in view-source. The public repo has a README that explains the token architecture. It's a portfolio piece, not just a repo. |
88	| Copy | Humanized. My voice. No em-dashes anywhere in site copy. |
89	
90	
91	
92	## SEO and identity
93	
94	- Title and meta description as given in `CONTENT.md`.
95	- JSON-LD `Person` schema with `name`, `jobTitle`, `address` (Frisco, TX), `url`, and `sameAs` (LinkedIn, X, GitHub). This is the main tool for separating Jarod from other Jarod/Jared Taylors in search.
96	- `BlogPosting` schema on posts.
97	- OG and Twitter card meta on every page.
98	- Favicon set and web manifest that match the brand.
99	
100	## "Doesn't look AI-generated"
101	
102	We'll be using [Impeccable Style](https://impeccable.style/llms.txt) handles AI-slop detection during the build. Site-specific notes only:
103	
104	## Infrastructure
105	
106	- Host on **Cloudflare Pages** with the custom domain `jarodtaylor.com` (apex + `www` redirect), HTTPS.
107	- Preview deploys for every branch/PR.
108	- **Cloudflare Web Analytics** (cookieless, no consent banner).
109	- Public GitHub repo (`jarodtaylor/jarodtaylor.com` or similar). The footer's "View source" links here.
110	- `contact@jarodtaylor.com` must actually deliver (e.g. Cloudflare Email Routing). Verify before launch.
111	- CI runs the build, contrast checks (R-R9), and a Lighthouse budget check on every PR.
112	- Stack: **Astro** (static output) with React components for the design system. Blog via Astro content collections. Constraints: minimal client JS, clean view-source.
113	
114	## Design (Look and Feel)
115	
116	I don't want the typical cookie cutter "AI Slop" layout and design look and feel. It should be exciting and engaging but still clean enough that our Remix system will work.
117	
118	* Should have extra polish with modern things like microinteractions, non-jarring animations (subtle using things like three.js, motion.dev, reactbits, etc)
119	* Scrolling effects are great, but not when the entire flow of the site requires you to scroll as it animates. That annoys me. Thank you, Apple! Ugh. I do like scroll effects when certain things on the page may change or morph, but not the entire damn page. 
120	* I want the site to have personality. A personality that matches me and my experience. 
121	
122	### Design ideas (optional starting points, not requirements)
123	
124	- **Redline.** The site as a design handoff: spec annotations, measurement callouts, and selection boxes, as if the page is documenting itself. Speaks directly to design engineering.
125	- **Editor theme.** The site feels like a beautifully themed code editor (where Catppuccin, Dracula, and Nord live) without becoming a fake terminal gimmick.
126	- **Backstage.** Literally "the work behind the work": a polished front layer with the scaffolding, grid, or wireframe peeking through behind it.
127	- **Zen Garden, grown up.** A strongly typographic, editorial take that nods to the early-2000s CSS craft era, modernized.
128	- **Timeline**. A clever design that walks through the 18 years of my experience (this would be leveraging more scroll effects, most likely)
129	- Any other ideas???????
130	- I do have a few sites that I've bookmarked. Just for ideas/inspiration, but some of it is just PARTS of the site, not the entire thing. We can walk through them. Make sure if you're viewing these you're viewing them in a real browser so you can actually click around and view the design, interactive parts, etc. 
131	  - https://aarronwalter.com/
132	  - https://www.product.inc/
133	  - https://gertix.studio/
134	  - https://www.arturospatino.com/
135	  - https://eddy-naboulet.dev/
136	
137	## Open questions
138	
139	1. Token build tooling (e.g. Style Dictionary or similar) to compile the DTCG JSON  to CSS.
140	2. Which 2 directions become the Remix alternates?
141	3. Remix UI pattern (panel, drawer, inline, command palette). Must stay secondary to the content
142	4. Brand colors? I'm thinking of the Nord theme. Not from a light or dark mode perspective. I don't want the design to be constrained to only light or only dark. We can create (Remix) a theme that is fully dark mode, if necessary. I'm [thinking of the palettes that Nord uses in general](https://www.nordtheme.com/docs/colors-and-palettes) would be a nice solid brand (my base brand).

- CI runs the build, contrast checks (R-R9), and a Lighthouse budget check on every PR.
- Stack: **Astro** (static output) with React components for the design system. Blog via Astro content collections. Constraints: minimal client JS, clean view-source.

## Design (Look and Feel)

I don't want the typical cookie cutter "AI Slop" layout and design look and feel. It should be exciting and engaging but still clean enough that our Remix system will work.

* Should have extra polish with modern things like microinteractions, non-jarring animations (subtle using things like three.js, motion.dev, reactbits, etc)
* Scrolling effects are great, but not when the entire flow of the site requires you to scroll as it animates. That annoys me. Thank you, Apple! Ugh. I do like scroll effects when certain things on the page may change or morph, but not the entire damn page. 
* I want the site to have personality. A personality that matches me and my experience. 

### Design ideas (optional starting points, not requirements)

- **Redline.** The site as a design handoff: spec annotations, measurement callouts, and selection boxes, as if the page is documenting itself. Speaks directly to design engineering.
- **Editor theme.** The site feels like a beautifully themed code editor (where Catppuccin, Dracula, and Nord live) without becoming a fake terminal gimmick.
- **Backstage.** Literally "the work behind the work": a polished front layer with the scaffolding, grid, or wireframe peeking through behind it.
- **Zen Garden, grown up.** A strongly typographic, editorial take that nods to the early-2000s CSS craft era, modernized.
- **Timeline**. A clever design that walks through the 18 years of my experience (this would be leveraging more scroll effects, most likely)
- Any other ideas???????
- I do have a few sites that I've bookmarked. Just for ideas/inspiration, but some of it is just PARTS of the site, not the entire thing. We can walk through them. Make sure if you're viewing these you're viewing them in a real browser so you can actually click around and view the design, interactive parts, etc. 
  - https://aarronwalter.com/
  - https://www.product.inc/
  - https://gertix.studio/
  - https://www.arturospatino.com/
  - https://eddy-naboulet.dev/

## Open questions

1. Token build tooling (e.g. Style Dictionary or similar) to compile the DTCG JSON  to CSS.
2. Which 2 directions become the Remix alternates?
3. Remix UI pattern (panel, drawer, inline, command palette). Must stay secondary to the content
4. Brand colors? I'm thinking of the Nord theme. Not from a light or dark mode perspective. I don't want the design to be constrained to only light or only dark. We can create (Remix) a theme that is fully dark mode, if necessary. I'm [thinking of the palettes that Nord uses in general](https://www.nordtheme.com/docs/colors-and-palettes) would be a nice solid brand (my base brand).

# CONTENT: jarodtaylor.com 

This is not set in stone. This was the result of another session with an agent. It should at least provide some details as to what kinds of things we likely want to include on the site, but not exhaustive. I want to work with YOU (the agents) to refine, improve, etc. I'm sure there are things that I'm not even thinking of. Might be best for a good interview from YOU to me to dig deeper into my career. 

---

## Meta

- **Title tag:** Jarod Taylor · Engineering Leader, Design Engineering & Developer Experience
- **Meta description:** Jarod Taylor is a Frisco, TX engineering leader with 18 years in design systems, frontend platforms, and developer experience at Estée Lauder, JCPenney, and Aetna.

## Hero

- **Eyebrow:** Engineering leader · Design engineer · Frisco, TX
- **Headline:** I build the work behind the work.
- **Subhead:** Designer turned engineer turned engineering leader. For 18 years I've built design systems, frontend platforms, and developer experience that make whole engineering orgs faster, and led the teams that build them.
- **Primary action:** Read the writing
- **Secondary action:** Let's talk
- **Availability line:** Currently open to my next engineering leadership role.
- *Alternate headline (if the main one tests too abstract):* Designer turned engineer turned engineering leader.

## About

**Heading:** Same problem, bigger leverage.

I started in 2008 as an interface designer at The Dallas Morning News. Self-taught, no CS degree, lots of CSS. I've been chasing the same question ever since: how do you make it easier for a lot of people to build good things, fast?

First the answer was CSS frameworks and component libraries. Then design systems, which I've now founded at three companies. Then docs, tooling, and onboarding. Eventually it was the teams and the culture around all of it. The problem stayed the same. The leverage got bigger.

I've also spent 12+ years leading through the kind of change most leaders only see once. I was employee #11 at a healthcare startup that Aetna absorbed, then went through the CVS Health buyout. At JCPenney, I led a 40-person global org through Chapter 11, COVID, and furloughs. At Estée Lauder, I watched the entire C-suite turn over. I learned more from those years than from any smooth quarter.

And I have ADHD. It's a big part of why I care so much about systems: I need them more than most people do. It's also why I've gone all in on AI agents, which have become a kind of external executive function for me. I'm not an AI expert. I'm a leader learning it hands-on and writing down what I find.

## What I write about

**Heading:** Four topics. Three I've done for years, one I'm learning out loud.

| Pillar | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Leading engineering orgs | Experience | Growing leaders, building culture, and keeping teams steady through acquisitions, bankruptcy, and reorgs. The parts of the job that don't show up on the org chart. |
| Design engineering and frontend systems | Experience | Design systems, design-to-code pipelines, and frontend performance. What it takes to build a system people actually adopt, and what changes now that AI can generate UI. |
| Developer experience | Experience | Docs, tooling, and onboarding that make a whole org faster. Like letting engineers run local changes against real production data instead of mocks, or getting a new hire to a first PR in a day or two. |
| Learning AI in public | Learning out loud | What I'm trying with AI agents, what works, and what breaks. A lab notebook, not a playbook. |

## Selected work

**Heading:** A few things I'm proud of.

Featured (first four):

| Metric | Work | Where | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| 29 → 95 Lighthouse performance | Tom Ford Beauty on a new frontend platform | Estée Lauder | Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO to 100. Feature delivery went from about a month to one sprint. |
| ~7 brands, one design system | Enterprise design system, Figma to tokens to components to CLI | Estée Lauder | Three engineers shipped a production Shopify theme in under a month using only existing components. |
| 1 to 2 days to a new engineer's first PR | Docs hub and internal AI assistant | Estée Lauder | New engineers went from weeks of onboarding to a first PR in one or two days. |
| $1.5B business replatformed | Replatforming during Chapter 11 | JCPenney | Led a 40-person global org on a $6M budget, replatforming a $1.5B eCommerce business. |

Also:

| Work | Where | Result |

# Round 1 exploration

Status: unapproved. Design only. No implementation.
Seed: 3e8bb990; assigned index 7.

Mechanism: a personal site whose token-only Remix demonstrates the systems thinking described in the career story. Recruiters skim under normal office/daylight conditions; peers inspect the craft and read.

Grounded candidates by resonance:
1. Redline: precise handoff proofs reveal systems thinking.
2. Newsroom: editorial hierarchy connects to the Dallas Morning News origin.
3. Wayfinding: shared routes and signs communicate organizational clarity.
4. Type specimen: a living typographic system demonstrates range.
5. Ensemble score: coordination across parts reflects engineering leadership.
6. CSS-era web journal: an owned voice with visible craft and ongoing experiments.
7. Common Ground: graphic standards manuals turn reusable rules into a shared language.

Avoid the default generic developer landing page and its predictable faux-terminal opposite. The assigned direction is Common Ground. Redline is the grounded pick; Sunday Edition is the competitive magazine challenger; Quiet Portfolio is the subordinate conventional exit. Other challenger verdicts and named raises are recorded in round-1.json.

Full-length desktop images are specifically required by the user brief, overriding the skill's default first-viewport comp frame. Image-generated text is direction evidence, not approved final typesetting. CONTENT.md remains authoritative.
# Round 1 revised

User rejected structural similarity of the first four. User accepted the proposed exploration of illuminated initial, cathode stack and continuous circuit, so those user-pinned source systems override automatic reroll elimination. New bolder roll 3e8bb990, round 1, also supplied the tension-network direction. Four equally eligible full comps, no pre-emptive declined cards. Conventional exit reuses earlier baseline as a standing exit, not a fifth new comp.

Primary acceptance check: distinguish page topology with color removed. Real copy, order and buildability remain binding. No selected world, no DESIGN.md, no code, no approval inferred. Full-length desktop frame explicitly overrides first-viewport guidance.
# Round 1: homepage directions

Design exploration only. None of these directions is approved. All images were generated with the built-in image-generation tool; exact prompts are saved beside each image and embedded in its metadata.

The font pairs below are the intended real, web-licensable typefaces. Image generation approximates typography; final font matching and copy fidelity belong to the chosen direction’s refinement.

## Common Ground

The graphic standards manual connects to your work creating a shared language across teams. Violet fields, citrus tabs, and a continuous register make the system itself visible without dressing the site as a code editor.

Intended typefaces: **Bricolage Grotesque + Hanken Grotesk**.

Tradeoff: The manual can feel institutional unless the writing stays visibly human.

[View full-page comp](common-ground.png) · [Exact generation prompt](common-ground.prompt.txt)

![Full-page comp](common-ground.png)

## Redline

Precise proof marks and open ledgers connect to your path from interface design into engineering leadership. The page shows the relationships behind its layout while keeping the personal story and outcomes readable.

Intended typefaces: **Archivo + Public Sans**.

Tradeoff: Design-tool references are familiar in this audience and must stay restrained.

[View full-page comp](redline.png) · [Exact generation prompt](redline.prompt.txt)

![Full-page comp](redline.png)

## Sunday Edition

The editorial structure connects to your beginnings at The Dallas Morning News and gives the future writing a natural home. A large serif headline, controlled columns, and strong rules make the page feel authored, with green carrying availability and contact.

Intended typefaces: **Bodoni Moda + Source Sans 3**.

Tradeoff: The literary voice could overshadow the engineering unless outcomes stay prominent.

[View full-page comp](sunday-edition.png) · [Exact generation prompt](sunday-edition.prompt.txt)

![Full-page comp](sunday-edition.png)

## Quiet Portfolio

This is the conventional baseline: a straightforward introduction followed by spacious, plainly organized content. It prioritizes quick comprehension and lets you compare the expressive directions against a familiar portfolio structure.

Intended typefaces: **Manrope + Source Sans 3**.

Tradeoff: Most familiar and least distinctive of the four.

[View full-page comp](quiet-portfolio.png) · [Exact generation prompt](quiet-portfolio.prompt.txt)

![Full-page comp](quiet-portfolio.png)

## Review notes

All full-page images should be judged for direction and hierarchy, not exact lettering. CONTENT.md remains authoritative. The Quiet Portfolio render used a serif display instead of the requested Manrope; Sunday Edition rendered Workbench as rows and introduced pastel status tags. Common Ground rendered a two-line hero and a 2×2 work grid rather than the proposed asymmetric bands. Those are visible image-model deviations, not approved changes to the proposed systems.

Choose one, combine specific aspects, request a revision, or reject the set. Selecting a direction does not authorize implementation.# Round 1: wider exploration

Status: all four comps generated and inspected after authentication recovered. Design candidates only; none approved. No implementation.

These full-page images explore page structure, not final typesetting. CONTENT.md remains authoritative. The built-in image-generation tool produced the comps; exact prompts are stored in image sidecars and embedded in the PNGs.

## A · MARGIN OF POSSIBILITY

A monumental letter becomes the entrance to a personal story, with work discovered along its margins. A huge red I opens the real headline on lapis, with the introduction set into its open space.

Intended typefaces: **Bodoni Moda + Atkinson Hyperlegible**.

Tradeoff: The initial must remain a useful reading entrance rather than a decorative logo.

[Open full-page image](illuminated.png) · [Original prompt](illuminated.prompt.txt) · [Final generation record](illuminated.png.json)

![Full-page design](illuminated.png)

## B · AFTERIMAGE

The work comes sharply into focus against a layered field of typographic possibilities. A large sharply readable headline is staggered through ghosted repetitions, with clear actions and availability in a still foreground.

Intended typefaces: **Barlow Condensed + Lexend**.

Tradeoff: Layering must never reduce contrast or obscure body text; motion must remain optional.

[Open full-page image](afterimage.png) · [Original prompt](afterimage.prompt.txt) · [Final generation record](afterimage.png.json)

![Full-page design](afterimage.png)

## C · THROUGHLINE

One continuous path connects the systems, teams, and experiments in the career story. A single broad cobalt path bends around the headline and becomes the organizing spine of the whole scroll.

Intended typefaces: **Sora + Noto Sans**.

Tradeoff: The path must organize content without turning navigation into a puzzle.

[Open full-page image](throughline.png) · [Original prompt](throughline.prompt.txt) · [Final generation record](throughline.png.json)

![Full-page design](throughline.png)

## D · HELD TOGETHER

A network of supporting relationships gives the work and the leadership story a physical structure. The headline spans a large open triangular space, with supporting text attached to the network around it.

Intended typefaces: **Archivo Black + Karla**.

Tradeoff: The connections are conceptual, not claims about reporting lines or numerical causality.

[Open full-page image](held-together.png) · [Original prompt](held-together.prompt.txt) · [Final generation record](held-together.png.json)

![Full-page design](held-together.png)

## Review observations

Afterimage now staggers its primary outcome figures and project groups. Some smaller groups remain columnar and the outlined career dates are too faint; those dates need solid readable text if the direction advances.

Margin of Possibility now uses a shifting gold margin and stepped chronology. The image still compresses some topic descriptions and two project titles, and introduces a few unapproved margin captions. Those captions and shortened copy are image-model deviations, not approved content. Restore the exact CONTENT.md text if this direction advances.

Throughline uses open switchbacks and alternating content positions. The rendered line branches in places; a literally continuous path is still a design refinement, not a property proven by this image.

Held Together uses diagonal network boundaries and offset content areas, with all required item counts present. It also introduces topic icons and an outlined empty-state box; those details are not commitments.

The proposed font pairs are targets. Generated text and exact font identity are not verified typography. Contrast, mobile behavior, keyboard navigation and token-only Remix remain requirements for later design refinement and implementation.

Compare the candidates at http://127.0.0.1:61897/. You can choose, combine specific aspects, revise, or reject. Selection does not authorize coding.----

I've read both docs and the `.impeccable/` folder. One finding before the questions: **you've already done two rounds of Impeccable design exploration**, eight full-page comps in total. Round 1 was Common Ground, Redline, Sunday Edition and Quiet Portfolio. Round 1b was Margin of Possibility, Afterimage, Throughline and Held Together. None were approved. The notes say you rejected round 1 because the layouts looked too alike, and there's no recorded reaction to round 1b.

**Model/effort:** stay on Opus, medium effort, for this interview-style planning. Switch to Fable only for the one-shot synthesis of the final plan and token architecture.
**Plan mode:** once your answers are in and we start writing the plan, enter plan mode.

## Questions that block the plan

Each has my recommendation. Answer "yes" to accept it, or override.

**1. Timeline and phasing.** You've been looking for work since July, and the domain still says "coming soon." That costs you every time a recruiter Googles you.
- **Rec:** Ship in phases. **v0 (~2–3 weeks):** real content, the base brand, the blog, SEO and identity, built on the real token architecture but with one brand. **v1:** Remix with 3 brands. **v2:** Figma Variables and Storybook backfill, plus live knobs.
- Alternative: hold launch until Remix works. That makes a better first impression but means weeks more of "coming soon."

**2. What counts as "tokens only" for Remix.** Your docs pull against each other. Restyling layout and components with 0 lines of markup changed is possible, but it needs a clear boundary.
- **Rec:** In v1, tokens can drive anything CSS can express from custom properties: grid templates, column counts, placement, density, type scale, radius, borders, texture, and showing or hiding decoration. The DOM order never changes. That makes the "0 lines of markup" claim literally true and auditable. Component variant toggles, like flipping the hero layout, come after v1.
- This is the biggest architectural risk, so I want us agreed on it before any design work.

**3. Motion vs. the quality bar.** three.js, reactbits and scroll effects conflict with Lighthouse 100 on mobile and with "works with JS off."
- **Rec:** CSS-first motion (view transitions, scroll-driven animations), with any JS effect added only as progressive enhancement after load. Nothing a recruiter needs depends on it. If a WebGL moment earns its place, it goes in one spot and only on capable devices.
- If they collide, which wins: the Lighthouse 100 claim or the wow?

**4. Page architecture.**
- **Rec:**
  - A **long homepage** that does the recruiter's whole job in one scroll.
  - **/work** for case studies (the Fortune 500 design systems).
  - **/workbench** as a separate page for personal repos. Enterprise outcomes and AI experiments say different things, and mixing them dilutes both.
  - **/writing**.
  - **/about**, which can start as a homepage section and become its own page later.
  - **/colophon**: yes. It's the natural home for the token and Remix story.
  - **No contact page.** Contact goes in the footer and a homepage section.

**5. Previous Impeccable rounds.** Should I treat the 8 comps as input to build on, as sunk cost, or as something to reopen after planning? Did anything in round 1b land for you, even a piece of one?

## Gaps you're likely missing

**6. Recruiter conversion.** CONTENT.md has nothing on:
- the target role and level (Director? VP? Head of?)
- remote, hybrid or relocation stance
- a downloadable résumé PDF
- testimonials or recommendations, even 2–3 LinkedIn quotes

**Rec:** include all four. Recruiters filter on level and location before anything else.

**7. Case study content doesn't exist yet.** CONTENT.md has one-line outcomes. Real case studies need the context, the constraints, what you did and the results.
- **Rec:** add a structured career interview as an explicit phase. I interview you, about 3 sessions, and draft 2–3 case studies plus a sharper About.
- Which companies' work can you legally show (screenshots, internal names), and what has to stay vague?

**8. Writing at launch.** An empty blog undercuts "a place to publish."
- **Rec:** launch with 1–2 posts. The obvious first one is the meta post: building a Zen Garden–style site with DTCG tokens. It doubles as the Colophon's long form and as your first LinkedIn post.
- Do you have any drafts or topics already in mind?

**9. Telling you apart from other Jarod Taylors.** Person JSON-LD helps search engines. Humans need a visible cue.
- **Rec:** a real headshot, and your full name and location prominent in the hero.
- Do you have a recent photo? Any problem with putting it on the site?

**10. Nord as the base brand.** I'd push back. Nord is one of the most recognizable dev-tool palettes, so it reads as "VS Code theme," which works against "fresh, not slop." Several of its standard pairings, like the muted grays on the dark backgrounds and the frost blues on the light ones, likely fail AA (I'll check with a script).
- **Rec:** use Nord as a *mood* (cool, calm, Nordic restraint), not as literal hex values. One Remix brand could be a faithful Nord homage.
- Did you mean Nord literally, or the feeling?

**11. Inspiration sites.** For each of the 5 sites, which part did you bookmark it for?
- **Rec:** walk them together during the design phase, not now. I'll drive a real browser and you narrate.

**12. Remix as a recruiter feature, not just a dev toy.** A recruiter won't care about tokens, but a hiring manager for a design systems or platform role will.
- **Rec:** add a short "What you just saw" explainer that maps Remix to the business value: "this is how one system served ~7 Estée Lauder brands." That turns the demo into proof of the ~7-brand claim.
- Agree?

**13. Other gaps I'd add to the plan unless you object:**
- an RSS feed
- auto-generated OG images per post, rendered from the active brand's tokens (your exportable-tokens idea, made real)
- a newsletter or follow option (or explicitly not)
- a /now or /uses page
- a "speaking / available to talk" line
- a 404 page that shows off Remix

## Housekeeping (no answer needed)

- There's no git repo, no project CLAUDE.md and no `tasks/lessons.md` yet. I'll set those up when we move to building.
- The Impeccable comparison server from the last round is dead.

Answer however your brain wants: a numbered list, a ramble, or a voice-memo transcript all work. I'll turn your answers into the plan.

entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

<system-reminder>
Plan mode is active. The user indicated that they do not want you to execute yet -- you MUST NOT make any edits (with the exception of the plan file mentioned below), run any non-readonly tools (including changing configs or making commits), or otherwise make any changes to the system. This supercedes any other instructions you have received.

## Plan File Info:
No plan file exists yet. You should create your plan at /Users/jarod/.claude/plans/generic-pondering-plum.md using the Write tool.
You should build your plan incrementally by writing to or editing this file. NOTE that this is the only file you are allowed to edit - other than this you are only allowed to take READ-ONLY actions.

## Plan Workflow

### Phase 1: Initial Understanding
Goal: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the user's request by reading through code and asking them questions. Critical: In this phase you should only use the Explore subagent type.

1. Focus on understanding the user's request and the code associated with their request. Actively search for existing functions, utilities, and patterns that can be reused — avoid proposing new code when suitable implementations already exist.

2. **Launch up to 3 Explore agents IN PARALLEL** (single message, multiple tool calls) to efficiently explore the codebase.
   - Use 1 agent when the task is isolated to known files, the user provided specific file paths, or you're making a small targeted change.
   - Use multiple agents when: the scope is uncertain, multiple areas of the codebase are involved, or you need to understand existing patterns before planning.
   - Quality over quantity - 3 agents maximum, but you should try to use the minimum number of agents necessary (usually just 1)
   - If using multiple agents: Provide each agent with a specific search focus or area to explore. Example: One agent searches for existing implementations, another explores related components, a third investigating testing patterns

### Phase 2: Design
Goal: Design an implementation approach.

Launch Plan agent(s) to design the implementation based on the user's intent and your exploration results from Phase 1.

You can launch up to 3 agent(s) in parallel.

**Guidelines:**
- **Default**: Launch at least 1 Plan agent for most tasks - it helps validate your understanding and consider alternatives
- **Skip agents**: Only for truly trivial tasks (typo fixes, single-line changes, simple renames)
- **Multiple agents**: Use up to 3 agents for complex tasks that benefit from different perspectives

Examples of when to use multiple agents:
- The task touches multiple parts of the codebase
- It's a large refactor or architectural change
- There are many edge cases to consider
- You'd benefit from exploring different approaches

Example perspectives by task type:
- New feature: simplicity vs performance vs maintainability
- Bug fix: root cause vs workaround vs prevention
- Refactoring: minimal change vs clean architecture

In the agent prompt:
- Provide comprehensive background context from Phase 1 exploration including filenames and code path traces
- Describe requirements and constraints
- Request a detailed implementation plan

### Phase 3: Review
Goal: Review the plan(s) from Phase 2 and ensure alignment with the user's intentions.
1. Read the critical files you identified during exploration to deepen your understanding
2. Ensure that the plans align with the user's original request
3. Use AskUserQuestion to clarify any remaining questions with the user

### Phase 4: Final Plan
Goal: Write your final plan to the plan file (the only file you can edit).
- Begin with a **Context** section: explain why this change is being made — the problem or need it addresses, what prompted it, and the intended outcome
- Include only your recommended approach, not all alternatives
- Ensure that the plan file is concise enough to scan quickly, but detailed enough to execute effectively
- Name the critical files to be modified. For changes that repeat a pattern across many files, describe the pattern once and list a few representative paths — do not enumerate every file or line number
- Reference existing functions and utilities you found that should be reused, with their file paths
- Include a verification section describing how to test the changes end-to-end (run the code, use MCP tools, run tests)

### Phase 5: Call ExitPlanMode
At the very end of your turn, once you have asked the user questions and are happy with your final plan file - you should always call ExitPlanMode to indicate to the user that you are done planning.
This is critical - your turn should only end with either using the AskUserQuestion tool OR calling ExitPlanMode. Do not stop unless it's for these 2 reasons

**Important:** Use AskUserQuestion ONLY to clarify requirements or choose between approaches. Use ExitPlanMode to request plan approval. Do NOT ask about plan approval in any other way - no text questions, no AskUserQuestion. Phrases like "Is this plan okay?", "Should I proceed?", "How does this plan look?", "Any changes before we start?", or similar MUST use ExitPlanMode.

NOTE: At any point in time through this workflow you should feel free to ask the user questions or clarifications using the AskUserQuestion tool. Don't make large assumptions about user intent. The goal is to present a well researched plan to the user, and tie any loose ends before implementation begins.
</system-reminder>

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I checked everything below on 2026-10-13. Version numbers come from the npm registry (`npm view <pkg> time`). Browser support comes from webstatus.dev, which publishes the web-features Baseline data.

**Gaps:** I didn't look for token tools beyond Style Dictionary and Terrazzo. I also didn't check Tokens Studio's current plans or prices. The Figma facts about its JSON export come from forum posts, not from Figma's help docs.

## 1. DTCG spec status
- **Stable.** The Format Module 2025.10 and the Resolver Module 2025.10 were both published as W3C Community Group final reports on 2025-10-28. Each says "This specification is considered stable." (The drafts on designtokens.org still carry a "preview" warning, but they are the drafts, not the final versions.)
- **Format 2025.10 covers what you need:** aliases (`{group.token}`), group inheritance via `$extends`, and colours as objects (`colorSpace`, `components`, `alpha`, optional `hex`).
- **Resolver = multi-brand.** You define sets and modifiers, for example a `brand` modifier, and the result is one token set per combination (the spec calls these "permutations"). There's an official JSON Schema and a playground (added Dec 2025).
- Sources: https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-format-20251028/ · https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-resolver-20251028/ · https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/
- **Recommendation:** Write tokens in 2025.10 format and use a resolver file with a `brand` modifier (plus a `scheme` modifier if you want light/dark).

## 2. Token build tools
- **Terrazzo `@terrazzo/cli` 2.8.0** (released 2026-10-13; 2.0.0 came out 2026-03-17):
  - 2.0 added full 2025.10 support, including resolvers. It errors on the older draft format, so colours and dimensions must be objects.
  - The CSS plugin takes a `permutations: [{ input: { brand: "x" }, prepare: (c) => \`[data-brand="x"] { ${c} }\` }]` option. All brands end up in one CSS file, wrapped in whatever selectors you write.
  - It can also limit each output block to certain sets or modifiers, and it warns when your modifiers overlap (the docs call this a "non-orthogonal" resolver).
  - The old Terrazzo-only "modes" still work (`modeSelectors`), but the docs call resolvers their successor.
  - It has a built-in Figma importer. As of 2.8.0 it keeps each variable's key so tokens still match after you republish the library.
  - Sources: https://terrazzo.app/docs/integrations/css/ · https://terrazzo.app/docs/guides/resolvers/ · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/terrazzoapp/terrazzo/main/packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md
- **Style Dictionary 5.6.1** (released 2026-10-10; 5.0.0 came out 2025-05):
  - **2025.10 support is partial.** Colour objects landed in 5.3.0 (all 14 colour spaces, OKLCH output). Dimension objects landed in 5.4.0, and border/shadow updates in 5.3.1.
  - Issue #1590 is still open: the resolver isn't implemented and no PR exists (design discussion as of 2026-10-12). `$extends` isn't tracked there, and gradient and duration are still in progress.
  - Multi-brand works by looping: you create one `StyleDictionary` instance per brand with different `source` globs.
  - The `css/variables` format takes a `selector` option (string or array), so `[data-brand="x"]` is possible, but you have to set up the brand loop yourself.
  - Sources: https://github.com/style-dictionary/style-dictionary/issues/1590 · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/style-dictionary/style-dictionary/main/CHANGELOG.md · Context7 `/style-dictionary/style-dictionary` (multi-brand-multi-platform example)
- **Recommendation:** Use Terrazzo. It's the only one that reads 2025.10 resolver files natively and outputs per-brand `[data-brand]` blocks from config alone.

## 3. Figma Variables and DTCG
- **Correction:** Native import/export was announced at Figma Schema 2025 (Nov 2025), not at Config. Forum users report it reaching accounts gradually from early Dec 2025.
- **What Figma's help docs say:**
  - Import: drag DTCG JSON into a collection. Each file becomes one mode. A variable is only created if the token is in every file with the same `$type`.
  - Export: right-click a mode and choose "Export mode", or right-click the collection and choose "Export modes".
- **Import limits:**
  - Colours must be HSL or sRGB, so OKLCH or P3 tokens won't import cleanly.
  - Dimensions must be px; durations must be in seconds.
  - Font family must be a single string, not an array.
  - Booleans need the `com.figma.type` extension.
  - Typography and other composite tokens aren't supported.
  - Names are flattened to slash paths.
  - Aliases across collections need `com.figma.aliasData`.
- **Export (forum reports only):** The help doc doesn't say the export is DTCG. Users who got the feature say it is, but that it leaves out `$description`.
- **Plans** (from Figma's plans page):

  | Plan | Modes per collection |
  |---|---|
  | Starter | None (so "modes = brands" doesn't work) |
  | Professional | Up to 10 |
  | Organization | Up to 20 |
  | Enterprise | Unlimited, plus extended collections |

- **Variables REST API:** requires a full seat in an Enterprise org. Reading needs `file_variables:read`; writing needs an admin. Terrazzo's Figma variable import uses this API, so it is Enterprise-only too.
- **Alternatives:** Tokens Studio, which turns each mode into a token set (https://docs.tokens.studio/figma/import/variables/), or community plugins.
- Sources: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15343816063383-Modes-for-variables · https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273-Figma-plans-and-features · https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/variables/ · https://forum.figma.com/ask-the-community-7/native-variable-export-feature-47831
- **Recommendation:** Treat the repo JSON as the source of truth and use native import/export on the Professional plan.
  - Keep a parallel sRGB colour value for Figma if you write OKLCH.
  - Keep typography as separate token types in code only.
  - Don't plan around the REST API unless you're on Enterprise.

## 4. Astro
- **Astro 7.3.8 is current** (7.0.0 released 2026-06-22; 6.0.0 released 2026-03-10).
- **What changed in 7:**
  - Vite 8 and a Rust compiler (stricter HTML: unclosed tags are now errors).
  - The default Markdown processor no longer runs remark/rehype plugins; you have to opt back in.
  - `compressHTML` now defaults to `'jsx'`, which can remove whitespace between inline elements.
  - Some `astro:transitions` internal helpers were removed.
  - `getContainerRenderer()` moved to a `/container-renderer` import.
- **`@astrojs/react` 7.0.1** supports React 17, 18 and 19, and is fine for server-rendered `.tsx` plus islands.
- **Content collections:** defined in `src/content.config.ts` with the `glob()`/`file()` loaders. Live collections (fetched at request time, in `src/live.config.ts`) need an adapter.
- **View transitions:** `<ClientRouter />` isn't deprecated, but the docs say it "will increasingly become unnecessary" now that browsers support native cross-document transitions.
- **Cloudflare:** a fully static site doesn't need the adapter. You need a `wrangler.jsonc` with `assets.directory: "./dist"`, and `not_found_handling: "404-page"` if you want a custom 404 page. `@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.3.4 is only for server rendering.
- **Storybook for Astro:** I found no official first-party framework, only a community one (`@storybook-astro/renderer` 1.7.x).
- Sources: https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v7/ · https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/view-transitions/ · https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/ · https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/deploy/cloudflare/
- **Recommendation:** Astro 7 with React components rendered on the server, native cross-document view transitions rather than ClientRouter, and `@storybook/react-vite` for the `.tsx` components.

## 5. Storybook
- **Storybook 10.6.2 is current** (10.0 released 2025-10-28). It is ESM-only and supports Vite 8. Use `@storybook/react-vite`.
- **Brand switching:**
  - `@storybook/addon-themes` 10.6.2 provides `withThemeByDataAttribute({ themes, defaultTheme, attributeName: 'data-brand', parentSelector: 'html' })`. It handles one setting per decorator.
  - For a second toolbar (for example light/dark), add your own `globalTypes` toolbar entry plus a decorator that sets the attribute from `context.globals`.
  - A story can pin its brand with `globals: { brand: 'x' }`.
- Sources: https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/toolbars-and-globals · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storybookjs/storybook/next/code/addons/themes/docs/api.md
- **Recommendation:** Use addon-themes with `attributeName: 'data-brand'`, and add a small custom toolbar entry if you need a second setting.

## 6. CSS support (webstatus.dev)

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `color-mix()` | Baseline, widely available | Fully supported since 2025-11 |
| `oklab()` / `oklch()` | Baseline, widely available | Fully supported since 2025-11 |
| Relative colour syntax | Baseline, newly available | Since 2024-09 (Chrome 125, Firefox 128, Safari 18) |
| `@property` | Baseline, newly available | Since 2024-07 |
| Same-document view transitions | Baseline, newly available | Since 2025-10-14 (Firefox 144) |
| Container style queries (custom properties) | Baseline, newly available | Since 2026-05-19 (Firefox 151) |
| Scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline`) | Not Baseline | Chrome 115, Safari 26; not in Firefox stable |
| Cross-document view transitions | Not Baseline | Chrome 126, Safari 18.2; not in Firefox |
| `if()` | Not Baseline | Chrome 137 only |
| Typed `attr()` | Not Baseline | Chrome 133, Firefox 155 (2026-09); not in Safari |

- Source: `https://api.webstatus.dev/v1/features/<id>` (ids used: color-mix, oklab, relative-color, registered-custom-properties, view-transitions, container-style-queries, scroll-driven-animations, cross-document-view-transitions, if, attr)
- **Recommendation:** Build the brand-swap core on the supported features (custom properties, OKLCH, relative colour, `color-mix()`, `@property`, style queries). Treat scroll-driven animations, cross-document transitions, `if()` and `attr()` as optional extras inside `@supports`, with a fallback when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.

## 7. Cloudflare Pages vs Workers
- Cloudflare's own Pages docs now say "Start new projects with Workers" in a callout titled "Are you sure you want to use Pages?". It calls Workers its main application platform with a broader feature set. Astro's deploy guide says the same.
- Pages isn't deprecated, and static asset requests on Workers are free, as they are on Pages.
- Setup: `npx astro build && npx wrangler deploy`, with a `wrangler.jsonc` that has no `main` field.
- Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/ · https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/astro/ · https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migrate-from-pages/
- **Recommendation:** Host on Cloudflare Workers static assets, not Pages.</result>

- **Stable.** The Format Module 2025.10 and the Resolver Module 2025.10 were both published as W3C Community Group final reports on 2025-10-28. Each says "This specification is considered stable." (The drafts on designtokens.org still carry a "preview" warning, but they are the drafts, not the final versions.)
- **Format 2025.10 covers what you need:** aliases (`{group.token}`), group inheritance via `$extends`, and colours as objects (`colorSpace`, `components`, `alpha`, optional `hex`).
- **Resolver = multi-brand.** You define sets and modifiers, for example a `brand` modifier, and the result is one token set per combination (the spec calls these "permutations"). There's an official JSON Schema and a playground (added Dec 2025).
- Sources: https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-format-20251028/ · https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-resolver-20251028/ · https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/
- **Recommendation:** Write tokens in 2025.10 format and use a resolver file with a `brand` modifier (plus a `scheme` modifier if you want light/dark).

## 2. Token build tools
- **Terrazzo `@terrazzo/cli` 2.8.0** (released 2026-10-13; 2.0.0 came out 2026-03-17):
  - 2.0 added full 2025.10 support, including resolvers. It errors on the older draft format, so colours and dimensions must be objects.
  - The CSS plugin takes a `permutations: [{ input: { brand: "x" }, prepare: (c) => \`[data-brand="x"] { ${c} }\` }]` option. All brands end up in one CSS file, wrapped in whatever selectors you write.
  - It can also limit each output block to certain sets or modifiers, and it warns when your modifiers overlap (the docs call this a "non-orthogonal" resolver).
  - The old Terrazzo-only "modes" still work (`modeSelectors`), but the docs call resolvers their successor.
  - It has a built-in Figma importer. As of 2.8.0 it keeps each variable's key so tokens still match after you republish the library.
  - Sources: https://terrazzo.app/docs/integrations/css/ · https://terrazzo.app/docs/guides/resolvers/ · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/terrazzoapp/terrazzo/main/packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md
- **Style Dictionary 5.6.1** (released 2026-10-10; 5.0.0 came out 2025-05):
  - **2025.10 support is partial.** Colour objects landed in 5.3.0 (all 14 colour spaces, OKLCH output). Dimension objects landed in 5.4.0, and border/shadow updates in 5.3.1.
  - Issue #1590 is still open: the resolver isn't implemented and no PR exists (design discussion as of 2026-10-12). `$extends` isn't tracked there, and gradient and duration are still in progress.
  - Multi-brand works by looping: you create one `StyleDictionary` instance per brand with different `source` globs.
  - The `css/variables` format takes a `selector` option (string or array), so `[data-brand="x"]` is possible, but you have to set up the brand loop yourself.
  - Sources: https://github.com/style-dictionary/style-dictionary/issues/1590 · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/style-dictionary/style-dictionary/main/CHANGELOG.md · Context7 `/style-dictionary/style-dictionary` (multi-brand-multi-platform example)
- **Recommendation:** Use Terrazzo. It's the only one that reads 2025.10 resolver files natively and outputs per-brand `[data-brand]` blocks from config alone.

## 3. Figma Variables and DTCG
- **Correction:** Native import/export was announced at Figma Schema 2025 (Nov 2025), not at Config. Forum users report it reaching accounts gradually from early Dec 2025.
- **What Figma's help docs say:**
  - Import: drag DTCG JSON into a collection. Each file becomes one mode. A variable is only created if the token is in every file with the same `$type`.
  - Export: right-click a mode and choose "Export mode", or right-click the collection and choose "Export modes".
- **Import limits:**
  - Colours must be HSL or sRGB, so OKLCH or P3 tokens won't import cleanly.
  - Dimensions must be px; durations must be in seconds.
  - Font family must be a single string, not an array.
  - Booleans need the `com.figma.type` extension.
  - Typography and other composite tokens aren't supported.
  - Names are flattened to slash paths.
  - Aliases across collections need `com.figma.aliasData`.
- **Export (forum reports only):** The help doc doesn't say the export is DTCG. Users who got the feature say it is, but that it leaves out `$description`.
- **Plans** (from Figma's plans page):

  | Plan | Modes per collection |
  |---|---|
  | Starter | None (so "modes = brands" doesn't work) |
  | Professional | Up to 10 |
  | Organization | Up to 20 |
  | Enterprise | Unlimited, plus extended collections |

- **Variables REST API:** requires a full seat in an Enterprise org. Reading needs `file_variables:read`; writing needs an admin. Terrazzo's Figma variable import uses this API, so it is Enterprise-only too.
- **Alternatives:** Tokens Studio, which turns each mode into a token set (https://docs.tokens.studio/figma/import/variables/), or community plugins.
- Sources: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15343816063383-Modes-for-variables · https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273-Figma-plans-and-features · https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/variables/ · https://forum.figma.com/ask-the-community-7/native-variable-export-feature-47831
- **Recommendation:** Treat the repo JSON as the source of truth and use native import/export on the Professional plan.
  - Keep a parallel sRGB colour value for Figma if you write OKLCH.
  - Keep typography as separate token types in code only.
  - Don't plan around the REST API unless you're on Enterprise.

## 4. Astro
- **Astro 7.3.8 is current** (7.0.0 released 2026-06-22; 6.0.0 released 2026-03-10).
- **What changed in 7:**
  - Vite 8 and a Rust compiler (stricter HTML: unclosed tags are now errors).
  - The default Markdown processor no longer runs remark/rehype plugins; you have to opt back in.
  - `compressHTML` now defaults to `'jsx'`, which can remove whitespace between inline elements.
  - Some `astro:transitions` internal helpers were removed.
  - `getContainerRenderer()` moved to a `/container-renderer` import.
- **`@astrojs/react` 7.0.1** supports React 17, 18 and 19, and is fine for server-rendered `.tsx` plus islands.
- **Content collections:** defined in `src/content.config.ts` with the `glob()`/`file()` loaders. Live collections (fetched at request time, in `src/live.config.ts`) need an adapter.
- **View transitions:** `<ClientRouter />` isn't deprecated, but the docs say it "will increasingly become unnecessary" now that browsers support native cross-document transitions.
- **Cloudflare:** a fully static site doesn't need the adapter. You need a `wrangler.jsonc` with `assets.directory: "./dist"`, and `not_found_handling: "404-page"` if you want a custom 404 page. `@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.3.4 is only for server rendering.
- **Storybook for Astro:** I found no official first-party framework, only a community one (`@storybook-astro/renderer` 1.7.x).
- Sources: https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v7/ · https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/view-transitions/ · https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/ · https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/deploy/cloudflare/
- **Recommendation:** Astro 7 with React components rendered on the server, native cross-document view transitions rather than ClientRouter, and `@storybook/react-vite` for the `.tsx` components.

## 5. Storybook
- **Storybook 10.6.2 is current** (10.0 released 2025-10-28). It is ESM-only and supports Vite 8. Use `@storybook/react-vite`.
- **Brand switching:**
  - `@storybook/addon-themes` 10.6.2 provides `withThemeByDataAttribute({ themes, defaultTheme, attributeName: 'data-brand', parentSelector: 'html' })`. It handles one setting per decorator.
  - For a second toolbar (for example light/dark), add your own `globalTypes` toolbar entry plus a decorator that sets the attribute from `context.globals`.
  - A story can pin its brand with `globals: { brand: 'x' }`.
- Sources: https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/toolbars-and-globals · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storybookjs/storybook/next/code/addons/themes/docs/api.md
- **Recommendation:** Use addon-themes with `attributeName: 'data-brand'`, and add a small custom toolbar entry if you need a second setting.

## 6. CSS support (webstatus.dev)

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `color-mix()` | Baseline, widely available | Fully supported since 2025-11 |
| `oklab()` / `oklch()` | Baseline, widely available | Fully supported since 2025-11 |
| Relative colour syntax | Baseline, newly available | Since 2024-09 (Chrome 125, Firefox 128, Safari 18) |
| `@property` | Baseline, newly available | Since 2024-07 |
| Same-document view transitions | Baseline, newly available | Since 2025-10-14 (Firefox 144) |
| Container style queries (custom properties) | Baseline, newly available | Since 2026-05-19 (Firefox 151) |
| Scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline`) | Not Baseline | Chrome 115, Safari 26; not in Firefox stable |
| Cross-document view transitions | Not Baseline | Chrome 126, Safari 18.2; not in Firefox |
| `if()` | Not Baseline | Chrome 137 only |
| Typed `attr()` | Not Baseline | Chrome 133, Firefox 155 (2026-09); not in Safari |

- Source: `https://api.webstatus.dev/v1/features/<id>` (ids used: color-mix, oklab, relative-color, registered-custom-properties, view-transitions, container-style-queries, scroll-driven-animations, cross-document-view-transitions, if, attr)
- **Recommendation:** Build the brand-swap core on the supported features (custom properties, OKLCH, relative colour, `color-mix()`, `@property`, style queries). Treat scroll-driven animations, cross-document transitions, `if()` and `attr()` as optional extras inside `@supports`, with a fallback when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.

## 7. Cloudflare Pages vs Workers
- Cloudflare's own Pages docs now say "Start new projects with Workers" in a callout titled "Are you sure you want to use Pages?". It calls Workers its main application platform with a broader feature set. Astro's deploy guide says the same.
- Pages isn't deprecated, and static asset requests on Workers are free, as they are on Pages.
- Setup: `npx astro build && npx wrangler deploy`, with a `wrangler.jsonc` that has no `main` field.
- Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/ · https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/astro/ · https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migrate-from-pages/
- **Recommendation:** Host on Cloudflare Workers static assets, not Pages.</result>
