**Each figure frames it differently:**
- **Backstage** pads by 40 on every side (`-40 -40 655.65 582.31`). Its guides follow the outline's own edge lines (y = 73.6, 93.2, 164.3…), not the 14-division lattice.
- **Blocks** redraws the outline as absolute-coordinate front faces. It is the same shape, except the J's front face starts at `M286.3 164.31`, folding in the `h.08` step. It adds extruded side faces offset by (+20.56, −35.61), which is length 41.12 at 60°, and its viewBox `-10 -45.61 616.21 557.92` includes that depth. Its `pattern#lattice` is 41.12 × 71.22 (two rows of 35.61), which is exactly Clean's lattice: 575.65/14 = 41.12, and 41.12·√3/2 = 35.61.
- **Clean** draws the same lattice on canvas, scaled to page size by W/575.65.

So Blocks and Clean share the lattice, and Backstage uses outline-edge guides. One caveat: the outline is not exactly on the 14-division lattice. For example, 164.31/35.61 = 4.61 rows, so both comments slightly overstate the fit.

## 5. Differences a custom-property value cannot express

1. **Figure renderer:** SVG construction drawing (Backstage), SVG extruded assembly with lattice pattern and rail (Blocks), or a full-viewport canvas (Clean). These are different elements and a different JS module each, so this needs an enumerated `figure` knob.
2. **Figure placement model:** a grid item in columns 6/-1 (Backstage), absolutely positioned at 54vw on the right (Blocks), or a canvas behind the whole first viewport at `z-index:-1` positioned by JS (Clean). On phones: behind the name at .3 opacity, a block above the name, or a canvas bleeding off the top.
3. **Intro system:** a Peek state machine with an intro-plus-replay toggle (Backstage), a one-shot CSS build that skips via `finish()` (Blocks), or none (Clean). The sessionStorage keys differ, and only Backstage has the `[data-skip-intro]` button and the 4s failsafe.
4. **Peek-only DOM** in Backstage: the `.cols` grid lines, `.dims`, `dl.spec`, the `data-peek` / `data-spec` / `data-build` attributes, the redline `::before`/`::after` boxes, and the Peek toggle with `symbol#reg`.
5. **Resting animation:** the pen lap (Backstage), the hover pull-apart of the parts (Blocks), or the expanding light ring (Clean).
6. **Phone nav mechanism:** a JS aria-expanded button with an ≡ drawn in CSS, a `popover` with an SVG icon, or a wrapped second row with no toggle.
7. **Header structure:** Clean nests the info strip inside an absolute `header.site > .bar`. The others use a sibling info strip in a stage grid with rows `auto auto 1fr`. Backstage also centres the nav absolutely at 64rem and up.
8. **Hero text grouping:** stacked bottom-left in one column (Backstage, Blocks), or the name on its own row above a ruled 12-column details row with right-aligned socials (Clean). This needs a wrapper element and grid-column spans per breakpoint.
9. **Name markup:** Backstage needs two spans to force the 2-line break on phones, plus `white-space: nowrap`. Clean relies on `text-wrap: balance` with a phone-only size override.
10. **Tagline accent:** a partial span (`.hl` or `em` around "behind the work.") versus the whole tagline in accent. This is expressible only if the span always exists and its colour is a token, so the markup should always carry it.
11. **Cue:** none, icon-only shown at 60rem and up, or a labelled "Selected work" link. Needs presence and variant knobs.
12. **Status dot:** a real span (Blocks, scale-pulse `::after`) versus `::before` with a box-shadow breathe. This is unifiable, but the animation keyframes differ, so it needs a knob or one shared choice.
13. **Text transform:** Backstage sets nav, talk and Peek labels uppercase with +.08em tracking and the mono sentence case only for info and socials. The others never uppercase. `text-transform` can take a token value, but the per-element split (mono vs text face per role) needs role-level font tokens.
14. **Font axes mechanism:** `font-stretch` (Backstage) versus `font-variation-settings` (Blocks). Clean has no axes. Both can be tokens, but a token set must define both, with defaults `normal` and `normal`.
15. **Font loading:** Google `@import` (Backstage, Clean) versus self-hosted `@font-face` with preload (Blocks). This is a different `<head>` and `fonts.css` per brand.
16. **Talk button shape:** pill filled with accent (Backstage), outlined with 0.375rem radius (Blocks), or square outlined (Clean). Mostly tokenisable (radius, fill and border colours), but the hover inversion target differs.
17. **Below-fold `.next`:** inside versus outside `main`, paper versus pine-deep background, with or without an `h2`.
18. **Blocks figure semantics:** `role="img"` with a `<title>`, versus `aria-hidden` (Backstage) or a decorative canvas (Clean).
19. **Breakpoint values:** 48/64rem, 47.99/60rem, and 720/1100/1800px. Media queries cannot read custom properties, so one breakpoint set has to be chosen, or the per-brand layout handled with container queries and class switches.</result>

  - `section.hero[aria-labelledby]`: `h1.name#name`, then `div.details` (wrapping `p.tagline` with no accent span, `p.bio`, `ul.social`), then `a.cue > span "Selected work" + svg`
  - `section.next#work > h2`
- There is no figure element; the mark is drawn into the canvas.

**Where the DOM differs**
- **Hero container:** Backstage `section.hero > .stack` / Blocks flat `main.hero` / Clean `section.hero > .details` (the details wrapper groups tagline, bio and social only).
- **Header wraps the info strip:** Clean only. In the other two it is a sibling.
- **Phone nav:** Backstage uses an aria-expanded button driven by JS; Blocks uses `popover` with no JS; Clean has no toggle and moves the nav to a second row.
- **Peek button and skip-intro button:** Backstage only.
- **Name:** Backstage splits it into two spans plus `.dims`; the others have plain text.
- **Tagline accent:** Backstage `span.hl` / Blocks `em` / Clean none (the whole tagline is accent-coloured).
- **Status dot:** Backstage `::before` / Blocks a real `span.status-dot` / Clean `::before`.
- **Cue:** Blocks has an icon only (shown at 60rem and up); Clean has a text label plus icon; Backstage has none.
- **`.next` section:** in Blocks it sits outside `main`; in Clean it is inside `main`.

## 2. Palette, type, layout

| | Backstage | Blocks | Clean |
|---|---|---|---|
| bg | `oklch(17.5% .026 252)` slate | `#1633b1` cobalt | `oklch(.285 .058 170)` pine |
| ink / muted | 96% .012 240 / 76% .03 245 | `#f2f5fb` / `#c2d1f3`, quiet `#a9bcec` | `.965 .014 165` / `.84 .035 168` |
| accent | lime `oklch(90% .19 124)`, on-accent 22% .045 140 | persimmon `#f56333`, side faces `-h #d54c25` / `-d #af371c`, text `#fd9a73` | apricot `oklch(.81 .125 52)`, on-accent pine-deep |
| extra | guide 68% .09 232, guide-ink 76% .08 232, redline 71% .18 20, surface | edge `#071869`, paper-h `#c3d1ef`, paper-d `#93aade`, faint = paper 22% | pine-deep `.235 .05 172` (`.next` section), rule = mist /.28 |
| display font | Archivo, wght 820, wdth 62% (`font-stretch`) | Bricolage Grotesque, 800, `"wdth" 86, "opsz" 96` (via `font-variation-settings`), self-hosted | Funnel Display, 560 |
| text font | Schibsted Grotesk; tagline 500 | Atkinson Hyperlegible Next; tagline uses the display face at 700 | Funnel Sans 380; tagline uses the display face at 420 |
| label font | Martian Mono 400, wdth 87.5% (info, social); nav and talk are text 600, uppercase, +.08em | Atkinson 600, +.02em | Funnel Sans 500 |
| display size | 35vw on phones; `min(12.5vw, 21svh)` at 48rem and up; lh .82, -.02em | `max(3.5rem, min(9.6vw, 19svh))`; lh .88, -.035em | `clamp(4.5rem, .6rem+16.4vw, 32rem)`; phone `clamp(4.5rem, 25.5vw, 9rem)`; lh .84, -.04em |
| lead size | `clamp(1.625rem, 7vw, 2.25rem)`, then `min(2.6vw, 4.4svh)` | `clamp(1.5rem, .95rem+1.5vw, 3.4rem)` | `clamp(1.5rem, .9rem+1.6vw, 3.5rem)` |
| body size | `clamp(1.0625rem, .82rem+.42vw, 1.5rem)`, 44ch | `clamp(1.0625rem, .78rem+.42vw, 1.45rem)`, 46ch | `clamp(1.0625rem, .85rem+.5vw, 1.625rem)`, 36em |
| breakpoints | 48rem, 64rem | 47.99rem, 60rem | 720px, 1100px, 1800px |

**Layout at 390 / 1440 / 2560**

- **Backstage**
  - 390: 4 columns. The name breaks onto 2 lines (spans become block). The figure is absolutely positioned behind the name: 78vw wide, pushed right by 23.4vw, opacity `--mark-phone` .3.
  - 1440: 12 columns. `.stack` spans 1/-1 in row 1 and sits bottom-left (flex-end). The figure sits in columns 6/-1 of the same row, centred, `max-width: calc(var(--mark-h) * 655.65/582.31)`. Nav is centred absolutely; the Peek word shows; the spec card sits bottom-right.
  - 2560: same layout. The name is capped by 21svh.
- **Blocks**
  - 390: the grid areas run field, name, tagline, bio, social. The figure is a block above the name, height `min((100vw - 2·gutter)/1.1045, 40svh)`. Nav is a popover.
  - 1440 and 2560 (at 60rem and up): the text stays in the lower-left grid flow (`align-content:end`). `.field` becomes absolute on the right at `inline-size: var(--mark-share)` = 54vw, from inset-block space-m to the bottom. The cue arrow sits bottom-right. The name is capped by 19svh.
- **Clean**
  - All sizes: the canvas covers 100svh behind everything. The header is absolute. The hero grid rows are `1fr auto auto auto`, putting the name in row 2 and pushing it down. `.details` is a 12-column row with a top rule.
  - 1440: tagline 1/6, bio 6/11, social 11/13 right-aligned. The screenshot shows the name on one line.
  - 2560 (1800px and up): tagline 1/5, bio 6/10.
  - 390 (720px and down): the bar becomes `"mark talk" / "nav nav"`, everything spans 1/-1, hero padding-top is 15.5rem.
  - The canvas mark (`field.js`): on phones (`w < 720`) it is 1.2w wide at y 0.2h; on wide screens it is `min(0.6w, 1.25h)` wide and bleeds off the right edge at y 0.06h.

## 3. JS

**Backstage `hero.js`** (7.2 KB)
- Builds the bleed lines: each guide is extended 5000 units from both ends into `.mono-bleed`.
- Clones `.mono-line` as `.mono-pen`. CSS animates the pen as a 0.03 dash lapping the outline every `--pen-lap` 16s.
- Writes live readouts: the computed font sizes and families go into `data-spec` / `data-readout`.
- `timeVertices()` samples both outline paths at 301 points and gives each vertex circle an `--at` delay so it pops as the pen passes.
- A state machine sets `html[data-peek-state]` to `arm`, `on` or `leaving`, or removes it. The Peek toggle and Escape drive it.
- Intro: the inline head script sets `.js`, `.intro` and `data-peek-state=arm`, guarded by sessionStorage `jt-intro`, `?intro` and no-preference reduced motion, with a 4s failsafe. The JS waits for `fonts.ready` (capped at 700ms), runs show, waits `--peek-settled` + `--peek-hold`, then hides. Any keydown, pointerdown, wheel, touchmove or scroll triggers `settle()`, which applies a no-transition frame via `.settling`. It also runs the phone menu.
- Reduced motion: the intro is never armed, all transitions and animations are disabled, and the pen is `display:none`. Peek still works, as an instant cut.

**Blocks `hero.js`** (1.2 KB)
- Exits unless `.intro` is set. Sets sessionStorage `jt-r6-blocks`.
- Skip (keydown, pointerdown, wheel, touchstart) calls `.finish()` on every finite animation. On `load` it waits for all of them to finish, then removes `intro` and `building`.
- All choreography lives in CSS (`.building`):
  - The rail draws out from the joint through the `rail-reveal` mask.
  - Arrows draw then retract.
  - The parts travel linearly from ±(123.36, 213.67) along the 60° rail and both arrive at `--t-click` 1340ms.
  - Faces stay paper line-drawings on the field colour until the click, then a `step-end` switch fills them with colour.
  - On the click the assembly scales to 1.022, three click strokes appear, and the rail opacity eases from .8 to .34.
  - Text rises in a stagger; the name is never animated.
- Hover (when hover is available and motion is allowed): the parts pull apart by (10.28, 17.8).
- Reduced motion: the head script never adds `.intro`, the status pulse `::after` is gated off, and the hover pull is gated off.

**Clean `field.js`** (4.9 KB)
- A canvas 2D lattice: side `s = W/14`, row height `r = s·√3/2`. Each vertex draws edges at 0°, 60° and 120°.
- Strokes are grouped by alpha quantised to 0.02. The base pass uses `--field-line` at .05 + .2 glow. Inside `clip(mark)` it uses `--field-mark` at .22 + .45 glow, then strokes the outline at .3.
- A ring of light expands from the mark centre every 9000ms, throttled to 33ms per frame.
- ResizeObserver (80ms debounce), IntersectionObserver and visibilitychange pause it.
- No intro and no session handling.
- Reduced motion: draws one still frame with no ring and listens for media-query changes. CSS kills the transitions and the breathe animation.

## 4. Monogram geometry

**The outline is shared.** All three use the same two path strings from `src/assets/jt-logo-icon.svg` (`M286.22 164.31h.08l-41.1-71.17…` and `m230.41 73.72 26.52.12…`) on base viewBox `0 0 575.65 502.31`. The header mark is the same in all three, though Backstage references a `<symbol>` while the other two inline the paths.

**Each figure frames it differently:**
- **Backstage** pads by 40 on every side (`-40 -40 655.65 582.31`). Its guides follow the outline's own edge lines (y = 73.6, 93.2, 164.3…), not the 14-division lattice.
- **Blocks** redraws the outline as absolute-coordinate front faces. It is the same shape, except the J's front face starts at `M286.3 164.31`, folding in the `h.08` step. It adds extruded side faces offset by (+20.56, −35.61), which is length 41.12 at 60°, and its viewBox `-10 -45.61 616.21 557.92` includes that depth. Its `pattern#lattice` is 41.12 × 71.22 (two rows of 35.61), which is exactly Clean's lattice: 575.65/14 = 41.12, and 41.12·√3/2 = 35.61.
- **Clean** draws the same lattice on canvas, scaled to page size by W/575.65.

So Blocks and Clean share the lattice, and Backstage uses outline-edge guides. One caveat: the outline is not exactly on the 14-division lattice. For example, 164.31/35.61 = 4.61 rows, so both comments slightly overstate the fit.

## 5. Differences a custom-property value cannot express

1. **Figure renderer:** SVG construction drawing (Backstage), SVG extruded assembly with lattice pattern and rail (Blocks), or a full-viewport canvas (Clean). These are different elements and a different JS module each, so this needs an enumerated `figure` knob.
2. **Figure placement model:** a grid item in columns 6/-1 (Backstage), absolutely positioned at 54vw on the right (Blocks), or a canvas behind the whole first viewport at `z-index:-1` positioned by JS (Clean). On phones: behind the name at .3 opacity, a block above the name, or a canvas bleeding off the top.
3. **Intro system:** a Peek state machine with an intro-plus-replay toggle (Backstage), a one-shot CSS build that skips via `finish()` (Blocks), or none (Clean). The sessionStorage keys differ, and only Backstage has the `[data-skip-intro]` button and the 4s failsafe.
4. **Peek-only DOM** in Backstage: the `.cols` grid lines, `.dims`, `dl.spec`, the `data-peek` / `data-spec` / `data-build` attributes, the redline `::before`/`::after` boxes, and the Peek toggle with `symbol#reg`.
5. **Resting animation:** the pen lap (Backstage), the hover pull-apart of the parts (Blocks), or the expanding light ring (Clean).
6. **Phone nav mechanism:** a JS aria-expanded button with an ≡ drawn in CSS, a `popover` with an SVG icon, or a wrapped second row with no toggle.
7. **Header structure:** Clean nests the info strip inside an absolute `header.site > .bar`. The others use a sibling info strip in a stage grid with rows `auto auto 1fr`. Backstage also centres the nav absolutely at 64rem and up.
8. **Hero text grouping:** stacked bottom-left in one column (Backstage, Blocks), or the name on its own row above a ruled 12-column details row with right-aligned socials (Clean). This needs a wrapper element and grid-column spans per breakpoint.
9. **Name markup:** Backstage needs two spans to force the 2-line break on phones, plus `white-space: nowrap`. Clean relies on `text-wrap: balance` with a phone-only size override.
10. **Tagline accent:** a partial span (`.hl` or `em` around "behind the work.") versus the whole tagline in accent. This is expressible only if the span always exists and its colour is a token, so the markup should always carry it.
11. **Cue:** none, icon-only shown at 60rem and up, or a labelled "Selected work" link. Needs presence and variant knobs.
12. **Status dot:** a real span (Blocks, scale-pulse `::after`) versus `::before` with a box-shadow breathe. This is unifiable, but the animation keyframes differ, so it needs a knob or one shared choice.
13. **Text transform:** Backstage sets nav, talk and Peek labels uppercase with +.08em tracking and the mono sentence case only for info and socials. The others never uppercase. `text-transform` can take a token value, but the per-element split (mono vs text face per role) needs role-level font tokens.
14. **Font axes mechanism:** `font-stretch` (Backstage) versus `font-variation-settings` (Blocks). Clean has no axes. Both can be tokens, but a token set must define both, with defaults `normal` and `normal`.
15. **Font loading:** Google `@import` (Backstage, Clean) versus self-hosted `@font-face` with preload (Blocks). This is a different `<head>` and `fonts.css` per brand.
16. **Talk button shape:** pill filled with accent (Backstage), outlined with 0.375rem radius (Blocks), or square outlined (Clean). Mostly tokenisable (radius, fill and border colours), but the hover inversion target differs.
17. **Below-fold `.next`:** inside versus outside `main`, paper versus pine-deep background, with or without an `h2`.
18. **Blocks figure semantics:** `role="img"` with a `<title>`, versus `aria-hidden` (Backstage) or a decorative canvas (Clean).
19. **Breakpoint values:** 48/64rem, 47.99/60rem, and 720/1100/1800px. Media queries cannot read custom properties, so one breakpoint set has to be chosen, or the per-brand layout handled with container queries and class switches.</result>

# Remix smoke test: three brands from one markup

The master plan is in `docs/PLAN.md` and was not changed. This file covers Phase 1, step 4.

## Context

- Jarod locked three brands on 2026-10-24:
  - **Backstage-lite** is the default (`prototypes/r6-backstage/`).
  - **Building blocks** (`r6-blocks/`) and **Clean and sharp** (`r6-clean/`) are Remix brands.
- Each prototype has its own markup. Remix needs **one** markup, restyled only by tokens.
- Per the 2026-10-14 decision, the winner is rebuilt on the real token pipeline in `src/`, and that rebuild **is** the smoke test. So there is no merged throwaway prototype.
- Scope: the header, the info strip and the hero (first viewport) at 390, 1440 and 2560. Sections below the fold come later.
- **Done when:** `/?brand=default|blocks|clean` matches each approved prototype, and every gate passes:
  - markup invariance
  - contrast
  - tokens-only lint
  - a11y
  - Lighthouse budget

## Decisions this plan makes (logged in DECISIONS.md on approval)

1. **Superset figure DOM.** All three figures are always in the page, and the knob `--hero-figure: construction | isometric | lattice` shows one of them through a container style query.
   - The three figures are `svg.mono`, `svg.build` and `canvas.field`.
   - This keeps each approved look pixel-faithful. Redrawing them as one shared SVG would be a redesign and need another review round.
   - Hidden figures cost only a few KB of SVG.
2. **Every figure is `aria-hidden`.** The `h1` carries the name, because ARIA is DOM and has to be the same in every brand.
3. **Peek works in all brands** (Jarod, 2026-10-24).
   - The readouts show each brand's own tokens.
   - The readout values are written by JS, so they would change the DOM per brand. They live under `[data-remix-ui]`, which the invariance test already strips, and the Colophon says so.
4. **Runtime state goes on `<html>`, never in `<body>`.** That covers `data-peek-state`, `.intro`, `.building` and `.settling`.
5. **One breakpoint set: 48rem, 64rem and 112rem.**
   - Media queries can't read tokens, so each brand's layout differences become enum knobs read inside these breakpoints.
   - Blocks used 60rem and Clean used 720/1100/1800px. Both get re-fitted to this set.
6. **Enum knobs**, each with `$extensions.com.jarodtaylor.enum`, validated in `derive()`:
   - `hero-figure`: `construction | isometric | lattice`
   - `hero-layout`: `stack` (Backstage, Blocks) | `name-over-details` (Clean)
   - `hero-intro`: `peek | assemble | none`
   - `nav-mode`: `toggle | wrap`. There is one phone nav element, a `popover` with a button. `wrap` hides the button and lays the list out as a second row.
   - `hero-cue`: `none | icon | labelled`
   - `talk-style`: `pill-fill | outline`
   - `label-case`: `upper | none`
   - Layout reflow through enum knobs is the v1 mechanism the master plan names. It doesn't contradict the "hero layout variants are later" decision, because that decision meant layout variants that change the DOM.
7. **The DOM always carries the superset.** That means:
   - the tagline accent `<span>`
   - the name split into two spans
   - the status dot as a real span
   - the `.details` wrapper
   - the cue link
   - the Peek toggle, plus the `.cols` / `.dims` / `dl.spec` markup
8. **Fonts have three roles: `display`, `text` and `label`.**
   - The current `body/display/mono` roles are renamed.
   - Each role gets a family, a weight, and one `font-variation-settings` token. The default value is `normal`, and it carries axes such as `wdth` and `opsz`.
   - The default brand's fonts (Archivo, Schibsted Grotesk, Martian Mono) are self-hosted, subset and preloaded.
   - The Blocks fonts (Bricolage, Atkinson Next) and the Clean fonts (Funnel Display and Sans) are injected lazily as `<link>`s when that brand turns on. The invariance test already excludes those links.
9. **One sessionStorage key (`jt-intro`) and one reduced-motion policy.**
   - With reduced motion there is no intro and no ambient motion: the pen lap, the hover pull-apart and the ring pulse are all off.
   - Peek still works with reduced motion, as an instant cut.
10. **The placeholder `alt` brand is replaced** by `blocks` and `clean`.

## Build steps (each step ends green on `pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm check`)

**Step 0: Fable cold-read gate**
- This is the adversarial gate that was due before the brand lock.
- A `model: fable` subagent reads this plan, the three prototypes and the token rules, then returns blocking risks only.
- Any plan changes it causes come back to Jarod before Step 1.

**Step 1: Extend `derive()` and the knob schema** (Opus subagent; `scripts/derive.ts`, `derive.test.ts`)
- Map every prototype color to the nearest ramp step first.
  - If lime, cobalt or apricot miss, add accent and neutral **lightness anchor** knobs.
  - Add the extra roles the brands need, e.g. Blocks' paper side faces and Backstage's guide color, as `figure.*` semantic roles.
- Fluid sizing is the largest hidden scope.
  - Stylelint allows only `%` and `fr` in component CSS, so values like `min(12.5vw, 21svh)` need knobs (display vw share, svh cap, figure share). `derive()` turns those knobs into `clamp()`/`min()` primitives, and they surface as `hero.*` semantic tokens.
  - Unit tests check that the output is deterministic and monotonic.
- Add the font roles, axes and enum validation.

**Step 2: Three knob files and the resolver** (`tokens/knobs/{default,blocks,clean}.json`, `tokens/resolver.json`)
- Delete `alt.json`.
- Run `pnpm tokens`.
- `check:contrast` runs **before any styling**, on the risky pairs, e.g. `#a9bcec` on `#1633b1` and apricot text on pine. If a pair fails, fix the knob, and tell Jarod if the change is visible.

**Step 3: Semantic and component tokens** (`tokens/semantic/*.json`, plus a new `tokens/component/{header,hero,figure}.json`)
- These are aliases only.

**Step 4: Components, default brand only** (Opus subagent)
- Build:
  - `src/components/Header/`: mark, nav and phone popover, Peek toggle, Let's talk
  - `InfoStrip/`
  - `Hero/`: name, tagline, bio, socials, cue and the three figures
  - `Peek/`: the spec layer
- Commit the untracked `src/assets/jt-logo-icon.svg` as the single source of the monogram paths.

# Remix smoke test: three brands from one markup

## Context

- Scope: the header, the info strip and the hero (first viewport) at 390, 1440 and 2560. Sections below the fold come later.
- **Done when:** `/?brand=default|blocks|clean` matches each approved prototype, and every gate passes:
  - markup invariance
  - contrast
  - tokens-only lint
  - a11y
  - Lighthouse budget

## Decisions this plan makes (logged in DECISIONS.md on approval)

1. **Superset figure DOM.** All three figures are always in the page, and the knob `--hero-figure: construction | isometric | lattice` shows one of them through a container style query.
   - The three figures are `svg.mono`, `svg.build` and `canvas.field`.
   - This keeps each approved look pixel-faithful. Redrawing them as one shared SVG would be a redesign and need another review round.
   - Hidden figures cost only a few KB of SVG.
2. **Every figure is `aria-hidden`.** The `h1` carries the name, because ARIA is DOM and has to be the same in every brand.
3. **Peek works in all brands** (Jarod, 2026-10-24).
   - The readouts show each brand's own tokens.
   - The readout values are written by JS, so they would change the DOM per brand. They live under `[data-remix-ui]`, which the invariance test already strips, and the Colophon says so.
4. **Runtime state goes on `<html>`, never in `<body>`.** That covers `data-peek-state`, `.intro`, `.building` and `.settling`.
5. **One breakpoint set: 48rem, 64rem and 112rem.**
   - Media queries can't read tokens, so each brand's layout differences become enum knobs read inside these breakpoints.
   - Blocks used 60rem and Clean used 720/1100/1800px. Both get re-fitted to this set.
6. **Enum knobs**, each with `$extensions.com.jarodtaylor.enum`, validated in `derive()`:
   - `hero-figure`: `construction | isometric | lattice`
   - `hero-layout`: `stack` (Backstage, Blocks) | `name-over-details` (Clean)
   - `hero-intro`: `peek | assemble | none`
   - `nav-mode`: `toggle | wrap`. There is one phone nav element, a `popover` with a button. `wrap` hides the button and lays the list out as a second row.
   - `hero-cue`: `none | icon | labelled`
   - `talk-style`: `pill-fill | outline`
   - `label-case`: `upper | none`
   - Layout reflow through enum knobs is the v1 mechanism the master plan names. It doesn't contradict the "hero layout variants are later" decision, because that decision meant layout variants that change the DOM.
7. **The DOM always carries the superset.** That means:
   - the tagline accent `<span>`
   - the name split into two spans
   - the status dot as a real span
   - the `.details` wrapper
   - the cue link
   - the Peek toggle, plus the `.cols` / `.dims` / `dl.spec` markup
8. **Fonts have three roles: `display`, `text` and `label`.**
   - The current `body/display/mono` roles are renamed.
   - Each role gets a family, a weight, and one `font-variation-settings` token. The default value is `normal`, and it carries axes such as `wdth` and `opsz`.
   - The default brand's fonts (Archivo, Schibsted Grotesk, Martian Mono) are self-hosted, subset and preloaded.

# Remix smoke test: three brands from one markup

The master plan is in `docs/PLAN.md` and was not changed. This file covers Phase 1, step 4.

## Context

- Jarod locked three brands on 2026-10-24:
  - **Backstage-lite** is the default (`prototypes/r6-backstage/`).
  - **Building blocks** (`r6-blocks/`) and **Clean and sharp** (`r6-clean/`) are Remix brands.
- Each prototype has its own markup. Remix needs **one** markup, restyled only by tokens.
- Per the 2026-10-14 decision, the winner is rebuilt on the real token pipeline in `src/`, and that rebuild **is** the smoke test. So there is no merged throwaway prototype.
- Scope: the header, the info strip and the hero (first viewport) at 390, 1440 and 2560. Sections below the fold come later.
- **Done when:** `/?brand=default|blocks|clean` matches each approved prototype, and every gate passes:
  - markup invariance
  - contrast
  - tokens-only lint
  - a11y
  - Lighthouse budget

## Decisions this plan makes (logged in DECISIONS.md on approval)

1. **Superset figure DOM.** All three figures are always in the page, and the knob `--hero-figure: construction | isometric | lattice` shows one of them through a container style query.
   - The three figures are `svg.mono`, `svg.build` and `canvas.field`.
   - This keeps each approved look pixel-faithful. Redrawing them as one shared SVG would be a redesign and need another review round.
   - Hidden figures cost only a few KB of SVG.
2. **Every figure is `aria-hidden`.** The `h1` carries the name, because ARIA is DOM and has to be the same in every brand.
3. **Peek works in all brands** (Jarod, 2026-10-24).
   - The readouts show each brand's own tokens.
   - The readout values are written by JS, so they would change the DOM per brand. They live under `[data-remix-ui]`, which the invariance test already strips, and the Colophon says so.
4. **Runtime state goes on `<html>`, never in `<body>`.** That covers `data-peek-state`, `.intro`, `.building` and `.settling`.
5. **One breakpoint set: 48rem, 64rem and 112rem.**
   - Media queries can't read tokens, so each brand's layout differences become enum knobs read inside these breakpoints.
   - Blocks used 60rem and Clean used 720/1100/1800px. Both get re-fitted to this set.
6. **Enum knobs**, each with `$extensions.com.jarodtaylor.enum`, validated in `derive()`:
   - `hero-figure`: `construction | isometric | lattice`
   - `hero-layout`: `stack` (Backstage, Blocks) | `name-over-details` (Clean)
   - `hero-intro`: `peek | assemble | none`
   - `nav-mode`: `toggle | wrap`. There is one phone nav element, a `popover` with a button. `wrap` hides the button and lays the list out as a second row.
   - `hero-cue`: `none | icon | labelled`
   - `talk-style`: `pill-fill | outline`
   - `label-case`: `upper | none`
   - Layout reflow through enum knobs is the v1 mechanism the master plan names. It doesn't contradict the "hero layout variants are later" decision, because that decision meant layout variants that change the DOM.
7. **The DOM always carries the superset.** That means:
   - the tagline accent `<span>`
   - the name split into two spans
   - the status dot as a real span
   - the `.details` wrapper
   - the cue link
   - the Peek toggle, plus the `.cols` / `.dims` / `dl.spec` markup
8. **Fonts have three roles: `display`, `text` and `label`.**
   - The current `body/display/mono` roles are renamed.
   - Each role gets a family, a weight, and one `font-variation-settings` token. The default value is `normal`, and it carries axes such as `wdth` and `opsz`.
   - The default brand's fonts (Archivo, Schibsted Grotesk, Martian Mono) are self-hosted, subset and preloaded.
   - The Blocks fonts (Bricolage, Atkinson Next) and the Clean fonts (Funnel Display and Sans) are injected lazily as `<link>`s when that brand turns on. The invariance test already excludes those links.
9. **One sessionStorage key (`jt-intro`) and one reduced-motion policy.**
   - With reduced motion there is no intro and no ambient motion: the pen lap, the hover pull-apart and the ring pulse are all off.
   - Peek still works with reduced motion, as an instant cut.
10. **The placeholder `alt` brand is replaced** by `blocks` and `clean`.

content.text: Fable found nothing wrong with the brand direction, but the plan as written wouldn't pass our automated checks. I'll fix those technical points myself. Two calls are yours:

questions.question: All three brands use dark backgrounds with the same layout: name bottom-left, figure on the right. Fable warns Remix could read as a recolour plus a figure swap. What do you want?

options.label: Keep as approved (Recommended)
options.description: You loved these three. The figures, fonts and motion already differ a lot. We log it as intentional and add a light brand later in Phase 3 if Remix feels samey.

options.label: Make one brand light
options.description: Change Clean (or Blocks) to a light background now, before building. That means another design round on an approved look.

questions.question: The style checker currently blocks the CSS that Peek and the intro need: calc(), clamp(), timings and helper variables. How should I handle it?

options.label: Loosen it a bit (Recommended)

content.text:
Short answer: it's not Impeccable. It's our own guardrail, and I overstated it a bit.

**What it is**
- I wrote it in Phase 0: `stylelint.config.js` plus a small plugin, `scripts/stylelint-plugin-tokens.ts`. It runs as `pnpm check:tokens-only` and in CI.
- It enforces the Remix promise. All brand differences must come from tokens, so the "{n} tokens changed · 0 lines of markup changed" readout stays true.

**What it actually blocks** (correcting what I said before)
- `calc()` and `clamp()` are allowed. `calc(var(--space-3) * 2)` already passes.
- What fails:
  1. **Raw units** in component CSS. Only `%` and `fr` are allowed, so `0.3s`, `160ms`, `60deg`, `0.08em` and `12.5vw` all fail. Each of those has to be a token.
  2. **New custom properties** that aren't tokens. Only private `--_x` helpers are allowed.
  3. **Math inside private helpers.** `--_x: var(--a)` passes, but `--_x: calc(var(--a) * 2)` fails.

**Why it bites now**
- The backstage prototype has about 40 timings and some helper math, like the redline boxes and the pen timing. All of that was written before these rules applied.

**My recommendation**
1. Add **motion tokens** (durations and easing) so timings come from tokens. That's in the spirit of the rule, and it means Remix can change motion personality per brand.
2. Allow **math in private helpers**, as long as it only combines token variables and plain numbers.
3. Keep **raw colours, raw sizes and brand selectors** banned.

Net: the rule stays strict where it matters, and Peek can be built cleanly.

Brand range: logged as intentional, as you chose.

**OK to loosen the rule as described?** If yes, I'll fold this and the other Fable fixes into the plan and start Step 1.

cat >> docs/design/remix-merge-plan.md <<'EOF'

## Amendments after the Fable gate (2026-10-24, approved by Jarod)

These amendments override the matching parts of the plan above.

**A1. Markup invariance**

- Everything the prototype JS added to the DOM is now rendered at build time in the Hero component:
  - the bleed paths
  - the pen clone
  - the per-vertex `--at` timings

  This works because the mark is all straight segments, so the geometry can be computed ahead of time.
- At runtime, JS only does two things: toggle state on `<html>`, and paint pixels on the canvas.
- The invariance snapshot changes:
  - It blanks the text in `[data-readout]`.
  - It drops the `data-spec`/`data-tpl` attributes and the canvas `width`/`height` attributes.
  - The Colophon discloses this.
- No font names are interpolated into content. The face name goes in a row on the spec card instead.
- **One hero module** replaces the per-brand dynamic imports. All three prototypes' JS together is about 5.3 KB gzip.

**A2. Lint (Jarod agreed)**

- Add `motion.*` tokens for durations and easings.
- Allow math in private `--_` props, as long as it combines only `var()` refs and unitless numbers.
- Raw colours, raw lengths and brand selectors stay banned.

**A3. `derive()` colour**

- **N named ramps** instead of two: `color.ramp.{neutral,accent,guide,redline,…}`.
- Each ramp has its own lightness anchor and peak-chroma lightness.
- The ramps must reach L 0.175.
- Acceptance test: `derive()` reproduces each prototype's hero colours within ΔE00 ≤ 2.

**A4. Fluid sizes**

- Fluid sizes are `$type: string` tokens, for example `min(12.5vw, 21svh)`.
- Spike first that Terrazzo emits them unquoted.
- Fluid sizes are excluded from the Figma export.
- Each brand gets a phone value and a wide value, read inside the shared breakpoints.

**A5. Fonts**

- Self-host all three pairings, including Funnel. Browsers fetch only the faces in use, so no lazy `<link>` injection is needed.
- `@font-face` rules go in `src/styles/fonts.css`, which is added to stylelint `ignoreFiles`.
- **Metric-matched fallbacks** (`size-adjust`, ascent/descent overrides) for each display face, to keep CLS < 0.1.

**A6. Brand range**

- Three dark brands with the same composition is intentional (Jarod). A light brand is possible later.
- Add Blocks' tagline colour `#fd9a73` on `#1633b1` (about 4.7:1) to the risky contrast pairs.
EOF

'| 2026-10-24 | **Lint loosened slightly:** `motion.*` tokens for timings; private `--_` props may do math over `var()` refs and unitless numbers. Raw colours, lengths, brand selectors stay banned | Peek/intro need helper math; rule keeps its purpose |',
'| 2026-10-24 | All three brands dark with the same composition is **intentional**. Light brand maybe later (Phase 3) | Jarod loves these three; figures, fonts and motion carry the difference |']
i=s.index(next(l for l in s if l.startswith('| 2026-10-24 | **Remix merge plan approved**')))
s[i:i]=rows
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(s))
EOF
git add -A docs && git commit -qm "docs: fold Fable gate fixes into the Remix merge plan" && git log --oneline -1

The tool you're thinking of is **Terrazzo**, and it's already what builds our tokens. The real question is which layer Figma owns. Logged as Q8 in DECISIONS.md.

**How the tokens work today**
- Each brand sets about 29 settings, such as hue, chroma and base size, and picks which colour step plays each role.
- `derive()` turns those settings into full colour and type scales.
- Terrazzo turns the result into CSS.

**The catch:** Figma variables can't do that math. If Figma owned every token, nothing could generate the scales, and every brand would be hand-tuned.

**My recommendation for Figma → Terrazzo → CSS**
1. **Figma owns the brand settings and role picks.** A designer changes lime's hue, or which step is muted text, in Figma.
2. **The code owns the math.** On export, CI runs `derive()` and then Terrazzo, and checks contrast and invariance.
3. **The generated scales get pushed back into Figma as read-only swatches**, so designers see real colours. The Figma MCP script in Phase 4 handles that.

**What I'm checking now so Phase 4 isn't a rework**
- **px vs rem:** Figma's import only accepts px. Our size settings are in rem, so they'll need a px form.
- **Colours:** already sRGB-safe.
- **Fluid sizes and the CSS-only switches:** already flagged as Figma-excluded.
- **Font axes:** variable-font axis strings may not map to Figma. Phase 4 will check that.

Here's the plan for Figma-importable knobs. I haven't changed anything yet and will wait for your ping.

**What Figma's docs say (help.figma.com, "Modes for variables"):**
- Each imported DTCG file becomes one mode, so one file per brand. A variable is created only if its token is in every file with the same `$type`, which matches our same-roles rule.
- Supported types:
  - color: sRGB/HSL only
  - dimension: px only
  - duration: seconds only
  - fontFamily: one name, no arrays
  - number: optionally boolean
  - string: accepted
- fontWeight and cubicBezier aren't listed. Group-level `$type` isn't mentioned either.
- On export, `$description` is reportedly dropped, and they don't say whether `$extensions` survive.

**Minimal schema changes:**
1. Put `$type` on every token.
2. Dimensions become px. derive() converts to rem as base/16.
3. Durations become seconds.
4. Weights become `number`; derive emits fontWeight.
5. Easings become strings like `"0.16, 1, 0.3, 1"`, parsed by derive.
6. fontFamily becomes a single name. derive appends `"<name> Fallback"` (the metric-matched face, A5) plus a generic family. The generic comes from a new string enum knob per role: sans-serif | serif | monospace.
7. Role picks become strings like `"neutral.750"` instead of aliases, because ramp steps don't exist in Figma. derive still emits DTCG aliases. `type.family.lead` becomes `"display"` or `"text"`.
8. Fluid, variation, tracking and enums stay strings. Enum lists live only in derive.ts, so I drop the `$extensions` agreement check.
9. Descriptions move into derive.ts.

**Excluded from Figma:** only generated primitives.

**First step:** a round-trip spike through import, export, `pnpm tokens` and a diff.

Okay, so I have some feedback. Took me a while to go through things. Here's what I got. You probably wanna take this and distill it in a document in the project so we don't lose it, because it's a good bit. 

General Thoughts:

    •    Let’s change the top to be “Engineering Leader | Frontend Architecture, Design Engineering, & Developer Experience”. Or do you think that it should be all 4 of those simply separated by “bullets” or the square type bullets? It reads similar to what shows on my LinkedIn headline, but really, the idea is I’m all 4 of those things. I’m just not sure how I feel about this part. I like the idea of having those 4 things on the page, because it immediately tells them what my role has been, but from a design perspective, I don’t love it. Especially on mobile. Maybe it’s something we can have some agents explore as far as options. Maybe it belongs with my name and the text below? Maybe we just need to rewrite the sentence below to include these things in it? Not sure. Something to think about.
    •    I actually am starting to think my favorite design is #3 (clean and sharp). I’m assuming it doesn’t matter which one I land on, right? It’s a matter of choosing my default/base brand and that is what would load first. Something that I have wondered is since we aren’t saving the users choice… if they click on Writing, Work, About, Colophon, etc… they will end up switching back to the default brand, right? If that’s the case, I wonder if should save their choice in the browser until they close the tab? I don’t think it needs to persist in their browser or anything. Would like your thoughts.
    •    There’s a bullet between Frisco, TX and Open to new roles. I think we can actually ditch “Frisco, TX” from this. I’ll have this information on the About and most jobs are either remote today and/or they likely found me through LinkedIn etc. and already know where I live.
    •    For the socials, let’s make sure we get the icons for each (LinkedIn, Github, X, email/mail). Let’s also use text-transform: uppercase on these. We’ll have the icon to the left of each label. For X, we can do the X icon with @jarodtaylor as the text next to it, so we aren’t just showing an X icon with X text next to it. 
    •    The text that is at the bottom… the double “ands” bothers me and just doesn’t flow nicely. I was thinking we could change it to something like: “Designer turned engineer turned engineering leader. For 18 years, I’ve built frontend platforms, design systems, and developer experiences. I’ve also led the teams behind them.” Or we rewrite it in another way, just something that flows better. What do you think?
    •    I feel like the CTAs in the top right of the headers are a bit much. Especially, considering we’ll be adding another one for remixing and switching themes. Plus it’s just too much on mobile web. I’m wondering if we should either change Let’s Talk button to just a mail icon, or simply add the contact link to the main menu. Then, we would be left with Peek and Remix. Another option is to simply use icon only buttons (the peek one and then an icon for remix - maybe a sliders/adjust icon or something). Open to any ideas. Even just the Peek and Remix buttons with the text and icon would be better than 3 of them up there. Especially on mobile. 

Backstage Lite:

    •    Refreshing the page doesn’t reshow the animation
    •    Is it just me or does this one feel like the background is sort of bare? Like, I don’t know there’s just something that feels missing with the JT Monogram (with its diagonal lines) and nothing else compared to the other two designs (Blocks having the dots and clean having the lattice). Wondering if we should remove the monogram extra lines that we have and maybe put some other subtle animated background or something here. I don’t know. Just seems off. Let me know what you think. SEE SCREENSHOT. 
    •    The lines in the animation (diagonal and horizontal) that extend from the JT monogram still do not transition out. They just go away while everything else transitions out. In fact the “grid” lines actually transition out by height so I would expect these other lines to do the same, if they can. 
    •    Also, there looks to be a double line on the left and right of the JT monogram so it looks as if the lines don’t align with the monogram (mainly because of this weird double line happening). SEE SCREENSHOT.
    •    There’s an ugly Skip To Content button that appears and disappears here and there. I’m assuming this was for a11y but not sure why it would ever show up at all. SEE SCREENSHOT. 
    •    On mobile sizes is the monogram’s lines supposed to be faint (almost invisible)? Again, if we do away with these lines due to my comments above, it won't matter, but just in case  SEE SCREENSHOT.
    •    The hamburger menu is to the left of the Peek and Let’s Talk button (which I think we should remove as stated above. It also has the words Menu showing. It should be just the hamburger with no label (might be from a11y). SEE SCREENSHOT
    •    The hamburger menu items just show/hide. No transition. A slide out would be a little more polished. 

Building Blocks:

    •    Just like the Backstage Lite, the animation does not re-animate when you refresh the page.
    •    The colors are bright and I love the animation of the JT monogram. I am a little bothered by how close the layout is to Backstage Lite. It’s pretty much identical with a font/color palette change (with the different monogram animation). It might be nice to have some agents keep the same concept of building blocks (again, I love the animation) but try some other layouts or configurations. I love how different Building Blocks is from Clean and Sharp. 
    •    I don’t love how the navigation is is right aligned and bumped right up to the Peek and Let’s Talk buttons. I know I mentioned above just removing the Let’s Talk button anyway, but still not wild about the nav menu on this one. Maybe this one could have the nav always as a hamburger menu (slides out from the right - full height)? Or, move it to the center and change up the navigation appearance a little. It’s the same text with a hover/underline as all of the themes. Maybe something a little more fun that plays on “building blocks” with a hover animation or something. No clue, just spitballing here. Open to ideas. 
    •    I don’t really have a ton more to say about this one, mainly because any “gripes” I would have would likely go away if we ended up with a different layout. 


Clean & Sharp:

    •    As I said, I really like this one. The layout, fonts, everything. I even like the colors. 
    •     The JT monogram probably needs to come down on desktop (mobile web is fine) Right now it goes above the header’s bottom border. Should probably drop down one level of the lattice so it’s not overlapping with the header border. SEE SCREENSHOT. 
    •    This one doesn’t have a hamburger menu on mobile. The menu items fit where they’re at, but if we add any others it’ll get pretty tight. So we should go ahead and add the hamburger. 
    •    Everything else looks great.

content.thinking:
There's substantial feedback to process here. I'm planning to log it into a dated feedback document with each item, my recommendation, and status, then answer his open questions concisely—like whether the role line should be folded into the bio (worth having agents explore a few options) and confirming that defaulting to Clean is just the resolver's default setting, since that's the brand that loads first and gets preloaded.

For brand persistence I'm leaning toward sessionStorage (tab-scoped) with `?brand` in the URL taking precedence for sharing, even though the master plan mentioned per-visitor persistence—his tab-only preference is fine. I also want to drop the Frisco reference and update PRODUCT.md's brand commitments accordingly, use uppercase social icons with his preferred @jarodtaylor handle for X via inline SVG brand marks, and refine his bio draft—his version is solid, just tightening the "and led the teams behind them" phrasing slightly.

For the header, I'm recommending removing the "Let's talk" button and adding Contact to the nav (possibly linking to a contact section since there's no dedicated page), keeping two icon buttons for Peek and Remix with labels on desktop collapsing to icon-only on mobile, and having the nav collapse to a hamburger at tablet width—noting Remix itself is a Phase 3 feature even though its header slot exists now. For Backstage, the intro not replaying on refresh is intentional (once per session, with `?intro` as an override), so I want to flag this design choice and ask if he'd prefer it on every load instead of assuming repeat visitors would find it annoying.

If Clean becomes the default, Backstage should become the Remix brand experience—maybe dropping the bleed construction lines in favor of a subtle blueprint-style background like faint 12-column guides or a dot grid, something worth exploring alongside the Blocks layout work. I also need to flag a few bugs: the bleed lines don't actually retract on transition despite an earlier claim that they do, and there's a double-line issue at the monogram edges where the diagonal guides nearly but not exactly align with the outline, which needs either exact alignment or removing the duplicate. Lastly, the skip-to-content link appearing and disappearing unpredictably needs investigation—it's expected on keyboard focus, but it might be triggering from intro-skip events or page load flicker instead.

For other smaller items: the faint mobile monogram was a prototype choice and becomes moot with a redesign; the hamburger needs an icon-only treatment with aria-label placed far right; and I should sketch the menu slide-out transition. Blocks needs a layout refresh since it feels too similar to Clean—agents should explore new layouts while keeping the existing animation and nav ideas. For Clean itself, I'm thinking the monogram should sit one lattice row lower on desktop, with the hamburger handling mobile.

On the bigger decision, he's leaning toward Clean as default but phrased it tentatively, so I should ask him to confirm explicitly rather than assume—my recommendation is Clean as default with Backstage and Blocks repositioned as Remix brand variants. There's also the pending PR question: I think recommending he push now as a checkpoint makes sense, since feedback will likely shift things afterward anyway, but given he's the CEO, I should frame this as a recommendation rather than a decision.

This is complex enough to warrant a structured plan—write a feedback doc first, then ask the key open questions (default brand, intro replay policy, header CTA approach, role line treatment), and skip asking about brand persistence since sessionStorage was already basically his idea. I'll create docs/design/feedback-round7.md with an ID/item/recommendation/status structure, and also copy his screenshots from CleanShot into docs/design/feedback/r7/ so they're preserved.

# Feedback round 7: the three brands on one markup (2026-10-27)

This is Jarod's review of the Remix smoke-test build (`feat/remix-hero`, 4b2b2ac), written up with my recommendations. The screenshots are in [feedback/r7/](feedback/r7/).

Each item has a status:
- **Do**: agreed, just build it
- **Jarod**: needs his decision
- **Explore**: agents prototype options
- **Bug**: a defect to fix

## General (every brand)

| # | Feedback | Recommendation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | **Role line.** He wants all four roles to show: Engineering Leader, Frontend Architecture, Design Engineering, Developer Experience. He doesn't love the info-strip treatment, especially on mobile. Ideas: change the wording to "Engineering Leader \| Frontend Architecture, Design Engineering, & Developer Experience", use bullets, move it next to the name, or work it into the bio. | Have agents explore 3 or 4 placements with the copy in every brand. The bio option overlaps with G5. | Explore |
| G2 | **Clean & Sharp is his favourite.** Make it the default? | Yes. The default is one line in `tokens/resolver.json`, plus whose fonts get preloaded. Backstage-lite and Blocks become the Remix brands. | Jarod (confirm) |
| G3 | **Keep the brand choice across pages.** Today, clicking a nav link drops the choice and the page falls back to the default brand. | Store the choice in `sessionStorage`, so it lasts for the tab and is gone when the tab closes. `?brand=` in the URL still wins, so a shared link always shows the brand it names. The inline head script applies the choice before first paint, so nothing flashes. | Do |
| G4 | **Drop "Frisco, TX"** from the info strip, and the "·" before it. Location goes on About. | Agreed. Also update the location line in PRODUCT.md. | Do |
| G5 | **Socials:** an icon to the left of each label, labels in uppercase. X shows the X icon and "@jarodtaylor". Mail uses a mail icon. | Agreed. Use inline SVG icons that take the text colour. The icons are decorative, so the label stays the accessible name. | Do |
| G6 | **Bio rewrite.** The double "and" doesn't flow. His draft: "Designer turned engineer turned engineering leader. For 18 years, I've built frontend platforms, design systems, and developer experiences. I've also led the teams behind them." | His draft reads well and has no em-dashes, so use it. It also leads with frontend, which matches G1's ordering. | Jarod (confirm) |
| G7 | **Too many header buttons**, and a Remix button is coming. Options: Let's talk becomes a mail icon or a menu item; Peek and Remix stay as buttons with an icon and label, or icon-only. | Remove the Let's talk button. Add **Contact** to the nav, pointing at the homepage contact section (mailto until that section exists). The right side becomes **Peek** and **Remix**: icon and label on desktop, icon-only with an `aria-label` on phones. A slider icon for Remix. The Remix button reserves its slot now; the panel itself is still Phase 3 (Q4). | Jarod (confirm) |
| G8 | **Hamburger at tablet width** in every brand. 4 or 5 items won't fit, and Clean has no hamburger on phones at all. This resolves Q9. | One menu pattern for all brands below 64rem: a hamburger button with an icon only (its `aria-label` is "Menu") at the far right of the header, and a menu that slides out. Brands can still style it, e.g. Blocks as a card or full-height panel. | Do |

## Backstage-lite

| # | Feedback | Recommendation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Refreshing doesn't replay the intro. | This is how it was built: the intro plays once per tab session so repeat visitors aren't made to wait, and `?intro` forces it. Jarod decides whether it should play on every load. | Jarod |
| B2 | **The background feels bare** next to Blocks (dots) and Clean (lattice). Maybe drop the extra lines around the monogram and add a subtle animated background. [01](feedback/r7/01.png) | Explore. A "backstage" ground should come from the system itself, e.g. faint column guides and a baseline grid at rest, made from the real space and type tokens. That's more on-concept than decoration. Explore alongside Blocks' layouts (K2). | Explore |
| B3 | **The construction lines that extend from the monogram still pop off** instead of transitioning out. The grid lines already retract by their height, so these should retract along their length too. | Bug. The last fix covered the column guides and the dims, but not the bleed lines. Check frame by frame against the prototype. | Bug |
| B4 | **Double line** on the left and right of the monogram, so the guides look misaligned. [02](feedback/r7/02.png) | Bug. The guide diagonals run a few units off the outline edges; the outline isn't exactly on the lattice. Snap each guide onto the edge it extends, or drop guides that duplicate an edge. | Bug |
| B5 | An ugly **"Skip to content"** button appears and disappears now and then. [03](feedback/r7/03.png) | The skip link is required for accessibility and should only show on keyboard focus. Find out why it shows at other times (e.g. a click, the intro moving focus, or a flash before the CSS loads). Then style it per brand so it looks intentional when it does show. | Bug |
| B6 | The monogram is almost invisible on phones. [04](feedback/r7/04.png) | That matches the prototype (it sits behind the name at 0.3 opacity). Revisit once B2 settles. | Explore (with B2) |
| B7 | The hamburger sits left of Peek and Let's talk, and shows the word "Menu". [05](feedback/r7/05.png) | Covered by G7 and G8: icon only, far right. | Do |
| B8 | Menu items just show and hide, with no transition. A slide-out would feel more polished. | Covered by G8: slide out from the right, with an instant cut under reduced motion. | Do |

## Building blocks

| # | Feedback | Recommendation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | Refreshing doesn't replay the animation. | Same decision as B1. | Jarod |
| K2 | **The layout is nearly the same as Backstage-lite**, just with different fonts, colours and figure animation. Keep the building-blocks concept and the animation, which he loves, but try other layouts. | Have agents explore 3 layouts. Each has to stay on the same markup, driven by tokens and enum knobs only. That's the real Remix test, and a good demo of "different site, same HTML". | Explore |
| K3 | The nav is right-aligned and crammed against the buttons. Ideas: always a full-height hamburger sliding in from the right, or centred with a playful hover that riffs on building blocks. | Include it in K2. Each layout proposes its own nav treatment, e.g. a block-snap hover. | Explore |

## Clean & Sharp

| # | Feedback | Recommendation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | He loves it: layout, fonts, colours. | This is the candidate default (G2). | — |
| C2 | On desktop the monogram rises above the header's bottom border. Drop it one lattice row. Mobile is fine. [06](feedback/r7/06.png) | Agreed. Change the knob for the mark's vertical offset on desktop, snapped to the lattice row height. | Do |
| C3 | No hamburger on phones. | Covered by G8. | Do |
